edges.title: Decanonicalization requires role-separated sufficiency
edges.text: 1H.hs7W supplies the problem of preserving coherence after privileged canonical form or homogeneous internal law is relaxed. 1H.9gYl supplies an explicit decomposition into independently meaningful obligations plus tests of whether reduced carriers and the composite remain sufficient. Together they earn a relation neither parent earns alone: removing a canonical/global form is safe only when the task-relevant obligations that must survive are separated explicitly and the resulting reduced/decanonicalized carrier is tested for sufficiency and end-to-end assurance.
edges.removal:
without 1H.hs7W there is no noncanonical/heterogeneous-carrier pressure; without 1H.9gYl there is no role-separated sufficiency and composite-assurance gate.
Boundary: this is a structural design discipline, not a universal argument against canonical representations.

edges.title: Noncanonical continuity can be regenerated rather than stored
edges.text: 1H.hs7W supplies continuity through stable relations among locally varying carriers rather than one privileged global origin. 1H.L4ld supplies an explicit recurrent mechanism in which bounded local state regenerates task-relevant relations and is revised when stabilizing context becomes obsolete bias. Together they earn regenerative noncanonical continuity: a system need not preserve one canonical snapshot or origin if a bounded process can repeatedly reconstruct the relation that defines continuity while variation remains governed and testable.
edges.removal:
without 1H.hs7W the noncanonical carrier/origin distinction disappears; without 1H.L4ld there is no bounded recurrent reconstruction or scaffold-revision criterion.
Boundary: the claim is about preservation of task-relevant relation, not preservation of every historical state.

edges.title: Heterogeneous systems can share a durable interface without a shared interior
edges.text: 1H.hs7W supplies coherent function across heterogeneous carriers/operators without requiring one privileged form. 1H.qI2L supplies operation-preserving translation, durable external interfaces, evidence custody, and an explicit non-identity membrane. Together they earn a portability relation: heterogeneous systems can share a stable public interface without homogenizing internal law when claim-relevant operations are preserved and the evidence boundary travels with the interface.
edges.removal:
without 1H.hs7W there is no heterogeneous/noncanonical architecture to bridge; without 1H.qI2L there is no operation-preserving interface or custody discipline.
Boundary: interoperability does not imply mechanism, code or ontology identity.

edges.title: Minimal regenerative state should be obligation-partitioned
edges.text: 1H.9gYl supplies the separation of stable task structure, private/identity particulars, address semantics, residual detail and outcome authority. 1H.L4ld supplies bounded reconstruction-critical state and the requirement that retained anchors be revised when they block necessary change. Together they earn a criterion for compact recurrent state: retain only explicitly named roles whose information is necessary to reconstruct the target relation; leave history, particulars and implementation detail outside unless the stated obligation proves them necessary.
edges.removal:
without 1H.9gYl there is no explicit obligation partition or minimization discipline; without 1H.L4ld there is no recurrent reconstruction target or revision pressure.
Boundary: minimality is obligation-relative and must be re-tested when obligations change.

edges.title: A portable interface is a typed contract of obligations, not a shared representation
edges.text: 1H.9gYl supplies semantic role separation, obligation-scoped sufficiency and composite assurance. 1H.qI2L supplies operation-preserving translation, externalized public state and evidence custody across changing substrates. Together they earn a typed-interface criterion: a portable public contract should expose only the roles, operations and evidence obligations required for downstream use, while unrelated internal realization remains free to differ.
edges.removal:
without 1H.9gYl the public object lacks explicit role/sufficiency partitioning; without 1H.qI2L it lacks cross-substrate operation preservation and evidence custody.
Boundary: the contract is sufficient only for the obligations it explicitly names.

edges.title: Persistent correspondence can be regenerated from bounded state
edges.text: 1H.L4ld supplies identity/function through recurrent reconstruction from bounded state. 1H.qI2L supplies a durable public correspondence that can remain useful while internal realization changes, provided claim-relevant operations and evidence boundaries are preserved. Together they earn reconstructible correspondence: continuity may live in the ability to rebuild the same public relation from compact state rather than in retention of the original implementation.
edges.removal:
without 1H.L4ld there is no bounded regeneration mechanism; without 1H.qI2L there is no typed public correspondence or evidence membrane to reconstruct.
Boundary: repeated reconstruction must preserve the public obligation, not merely reproduce a familiar label.

faces.title: Decanonicalized systems need role-separated regenerative scaffolds
faces.text: 1H.hs7W contributes coherence under removal of privileged canonical form, 1H.9gYl contributes explicit role separation and sufficiency testing, and 1H.L4ld contributes recurrent reconstruction from bounded state plus scaffold revision. Together they earn a three-way architecture: a system can abandon one canonical representation while retaining continuity if a bounded, role-separated scaffold contains enough information to regenerate the task-relevant relations and is revised when pressure reveals that its former stabilizing role has become bias.
faces.removal: remove 1H.hs7W and there is no decanonicalization/heterogeneous-carrier pressure; remove 1H.9gYl and the scaffold loses obligation partition and sufficiency/composite tests; remove 1H.L4ld and the scaffold is no longer a regenerative process with revision conditions.

faces.title: Interoperability across heterogeneous carriers requires role-separated, operation-preserving contracts
faces.text: 1H.hs7W contributes heterogeneous/noncanonical carriers and governed invariance, 1H.9gYl contributes role-separated obligations and composite assurance, and 1H.qI2L contributes operation-preserving translation with evidence custody. Together they earn a stricter portability principle: shared use across differing interiors requires a typed public contract that preserves only the roles and operations consumed downstream and carries the boundary on what the correspondence does not identify.
faces.removal: remove 1H.hs7W and heterogeneity/noncanonicality disappears; remove 1H.9gYl and explicit obligation partition/sufficiency disappears; remove 1H.qI2L and operation-preserving cross-substrate correspondence plus custody disappears.

faces.title: Regenerated correspondence earns continuity only under noncanonical carrier variation
faces.text: 1H.hs7W contributes pressure-aligned tests across changing carriers/operators, 1H.L4ld contributes recurrent bounded-state regeneration, and 1H.qI2L contributes a durable public correspondence with its evidence membrane. Together they earn a validation law: repeated regeneration counts as continuity only when the reconstructed interface preserves its claimed relation across relevant carrier/operator variation that could expose false invariance, while the claim boundary is regenerated with the relation.
faces.removal: remove 1H.hs7W and the relevant noncanonical variation/stress surface disappears; remove 1H.L4ld and repeated regeneration disappears; remove 1H.qI2L and there is no typed correspondence/evidence boundary whose continuity can be assessed.

faces.title: The minimal durable state is the set of claim-relevant obligations needed to reconstruct a typed public interface
faces.text: 1H.9gYl contributes obligation separation and minimization under sufficiency tests, 1H.L4ld contributes reconstruction-critical bounded state, and 1H.qI2L contributes operation/evidence-preserving public correspondence. Together they earn a compact state law: durable state can be reduced to the role-typed operations, evidence boundaries and authority/scaffold information required to regenerate the public relation; implementation history and unrelated internal state may vary or disappear.
faces.removal: remove 1H.9gYl and there is no principled role/minimization basis; remove 1H.L4ld and no bounded reconstruction mechanism; remove 1H.qI2L and no operation-preserving typed interface or custody object.

volume.title: Reconstructible relational contract
volume.text:
Across all four parents, continuity and correspondence repeatedly detach from one fixed internal snapshot, but the higher-rank closure adds a stricter requirement than any proper subset. 1H.hs7W shows that coherence can survive noncanonical and heterogeneous carriers only when roles, regimes and pressure-aligned tests remain explicit. 1H.9gYl shows that stable task structure, private particulars, address semantics, residual detail and outcome authority should be separated into obligations whose reduced carriers must be proven sufficient. 1H.L4ld shows that functional continuity can be repeatedly regenerated from bounded local state, while the same scaffold can become an adaptation-blocking bias that needs revision. 1H.qI2L shows that a public correspondence can survive substrate change when claim-relevant operations and its evidence boundary are carried forward without promoting usability into interior identity.


The complete four-way closure is therefore a reconstructible relational contract: the thing that persists need not be a canonical representation, a complete history, or a shared implementation. It can instead be a role-separated public obligation containing the minimal operations, evidence boundaries and reconstruction-critical scaffold state needed to re-instantiate the relation downstream work consumes. The contract remains valid only while it survives pressure-aligned variation across heterogeneous carriers and while its retained scaffold is revised when stabilizing history ceases to be faithful.
volume.invariant: A noncanonical system can preserve task-relevant identity or correspondence through changing internal realization when continuity is carried by a role-separated relational contract containing only the operations, evidence boundaries and scaffold state required to reconstruct the public obligation; that contract may be regenerated from bounded local state across heterogeneous interiors, but remains valid only while pressure-aligned tests show the scaffold is sufficient and has not become an obsolete bias.
removal: Remove 1H.hs7W: the closure loses direct noncanonical/heterogeneous carrier variation and pressure-aligned governance; the remaining trio can reconstruct a typed interface but cannot earn coherence without canonical form under carrier variation.
Remove 1H.9gYl: the closure loses role separation, obligation-scoped minimization and composite assurance; the persistent contract becomes an undifferentiated interface.
Remove 1H.L4ld: the closure loses recurrent re-instantiation from bounded state and anchor-debt revision; the contract may persist as externalized state but not as a regenerative process.

Remove 1H.qI2L: the closure loses operation-preserving translation, evidence custody and the non-identity membrane; the remaining trio cannot earn cross-substrate public correspondence without shared interior.

metabolites.title: Preserve the obligations that let the relation be rebuilt
metabolites.text: durable state can be the smallest role-separated set of claim-relevant operations, evidence boundaries and authority/scaffold information sufficient to regenerate a public relation while unrelated implementation history varies.
metabolites.compression: Preserve the obligations that let the relation be rebuilt, not the whole interior.

metabolites.title: Port the relation through preserved operations, not one canonical interior
metabolites.text: cross-substrate continuity does not require one canonical interior or homogeneous law when the public interface preserves claim-relevant operations and its evidence boundary across heterogeneous carriers.
metabolites.compression: Port the relation through preserved operations, not by forcing one canonical form.

metabolites.title: Regenerate the boundary with the relation and know when the scaffold must change
metabolites.text: every regenerated/stabilizing interface should carry both its evidence boundary and an explicit revision condition because the scaffold that preserves continuity can later become an obsolete bias.
metabolites.compression: Regenerate the boundary with the relation, and know when the scaffold must change.

edges.title: obligation-scoped selective realization
edges.text:
1H.ujF6 supplies context- and trajectory-dependent selective actualization over a stable/reacquirable scaffold; 1H.9gYl supplies explicit semantic role separation and exact-obligation sufficiency. Together they earn a bounded architecture in which only the flexible state presently needed for a named task is instantiated, while the current carrier is tested for sufficiency against that exact obligation rather than treated as globally complete.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.ujF6 and the relation loses dynamic selective realization and pressure-indexed reallocation; remove 1H.9gYl and it loses the explicit role/sufficiency gate that says what the realization must actually support.

edges.title: actualization is not expansion
edges.text:
1H.ujF6 shows that access to useful behavior can change through selective realization, routing and reallocation as context or pressure changes; 1H.uSiP shows that improved access or visible performance does not by itself establish a larger reachable support. Together they require a distinction between re-realizing/reweighting existing possibility and genuinely enlarging it, with operating trajectory and boundary witness carried separately.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.ujF6 and there is no explicit moving realization/reallocation process; remove 1H.uSiP and there is no independent criterion separating better access from boundary expansion.

edges.title: selective coherence across noncanonical carriers
edges.text:
1H.ujF6 supplies bounded local actualization and revalidation as context and pressure move; 1H.hs7W supplies coherent relational continuity without a privileged global carrier. Together they earn the possibility that one task-relevant relation can remain coherent while its active support appears, moves or disappears locally, provided relation semantics and validity conditions survive each transition.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.ujF6 and the relation loses selective/path-sensitive local realization; remove 1H.hs7W and it loses the warrant for coherence across changing noncanonical carriers.

edges.title: sufficiency frontier is not capability frontier
edges.text:
1H.9gYl makes sufficiency relative to an exact downstream obligation; 1H.uSiP distinguishes success on a current task or measurement from expansion of the underlying possibility set. Together they establish that proving a reduced carrier is enough for task T does not show that the carrier preserves every possibility or that the system’s capability frontier has grown.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.9gYl and exact-obligation sufficiency disappears; remove 1H.uSiP and the independent support/expansion boundary disappears.

edges.title: role-stable continuity without carrier identity
edges.text:
1H.9gYl separates identity, role, address, residual detail and authority while demanding composite sufficiency; 1H.hs7W shows task-relevant relation persisting across heterogeneous or noncanonical carriers. Together they earn continuity through stable role semantics and tested relation rather than through representational identity, as long as the recombined carrier remains sufficient for the named obligation.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.9gYl and role semantics plus obligation-scoped sufficiency disappear; remove 1H.hs7W and cross-carrier relational coherence disappears.


zy — pressure-tested boundary change
1H.uSiP requires a boundary-crossing witness before calling an adaptive gain expansion; 1H.hs7W requires candidate invariants to survive variation along the coordinate expected to disturb neighboring non-invariants. Together they earn a stronger growth test: capability expansion across carrier or regime change must cross the old boundary while the claimed relation remains coherent under pressure-aligned perturbation.
Rank necessity: remove 1H.uSiP and the expansion criterion disappears; remove 1H.hs7W and the pressure-aligned cross-carrier invariance test disappears.

faces.title: selective realization with expansion accounting
faces.text: 1H.ujF6 contributes selective actualization and reallocation, 1H.9gYl contributes role separation plus exact-obligation sufficiency, and 1H.uSiP contributes the boundary between better access and enlarged possibility. Together they derive that a task-specific realized state may be both useful and sufficient without implying growth of the reachable support; any improvement must be classified as changed realization/reweighting or true expansion by a separate boundary witness.
faces.removal: without 1H.ujF6 there is no selective realization mechanism; without 1H.9gYl no exact task-sufficiency test; without 1H.uSiP no expansion distinction.

faces.title: elastic sufficient coherence
faces.text: 1H.ujF6 contributes context- and trajectory-indexed local support, 1H.9gYl contributes stable semantic roles and obligation-scoped sufficiency, and 1H.hs7W contributes continuity across noncanonical carriers. Together they derive an elastic carrier law: task function can persist while active realization changes locally if the role semantics and named obligation remain legible and sufficient and the relation is revalidated through each transition.
faces.removal:
without 1H.ujF6 elasticity loses selective/path-sensitive realization; without 1H.9gYl it loses exact role and sufficiency semantics; without 1H.hs7W it loses carrier-flexible relational continuity.


wzy — trajectory-sensitive expansion witness
1H.ujF6 contributes a moving pressure/frontier and adaptive reallocation, 1H.uSiP contributes the separate expansion boundary, and 1H.hs7W contributes pressure-aligned invariance testing across changing carriers. Together they derive that when support moves under pressure, an apparent gain counts as expansion only if it crosses the prior boundary under a relevant stress test while the task relation remains coherent; otherwise the gain remains a reallocation or access effect.
Removal tests: without 1H.ujF6 there is no moving realization/frontier; without 1H.uSiP no criterion for boundary expansion; without 1H.hs7W no pressure-aligned relational witness across carrier variation.


xzy — role-stable boundary revision
1H.9gYl contributes stable independently meaningful roles and exact obligation, 1H.uSiP contributes the distinction between current success and support expansion, and 1H.hs7W contributes relational continuity across heterogeneous carriers. Together they derive that before/after claims across adaptation are commensurable only when role semantics remain stable enough to compare, the exact obligation remains testable, and any claimed boundary change is separately witnessed across the relevant carrier/regime variation.
Removal tests: without 1H.9gYl semantic comparability and exact obligation disappear; without 1H.uSiP the expansion test disappears; without 1H.hs7W coherent comparison across carrier change disappears.

volume.title: boundary-audited elastic continuity
volume.invariant: Continuity through changing realization is warranted when the carrier may elastically change but the named obligation, role semantics, relational coherence and regime/trajectory evidence remain testable; apparent improvement remains an access/reallocation claim until a separate boundary-crossing witness earns expansion, and an earned boundary change triggers fresh continuity warrant rather than automatic inheritance.

metabolites.title: ACCESS-IS-NOT-EXPANSION
metabolites.text: selective actualization, reweighting or adaptive reallocation can improve visible capability without enlarging reachable support; expansion requires evidence that crosses the explicitly named prior boundary.
metabolites.compression: better access to capacity is not yet more capacity.

metabolites.title: ROLE-STABLE-ELASTIC-CARRIER
metabolites.text: the active carrier may change, appear locally or be selectively reconstructed while continuity persists, provided named role semantics and the exact task obligation remain sufficient and the relation is revalidated through the transition.
metabolites.compression: change the carrier; keep the obligation and relation legible.

metabolites.title: BOUNDARY-TRIGGERED-REWARRANT
metabolites.text: when adaptation is claimed to cross a capability or support boundary, the previous continuity warrant becomes historical provenance rather than automatic authorization for the new state; the changed realization must re-earn sufficiency, role stability and relational coherence under the new typed regime.
metabolites.compression: crossing the boundary expires inherited warrant; growth must re-earn continuity.

edges.title: Semantic continuity across changing local context needs explicit transition law
edges.text: S.sMNy supplies the case where local frames are arbitrary and the same geometrical object survives only because feature components and operators transform lawfully between gauges. S.lul4 supplies a context lifecycle in which active state is repeatedly selected, summarized, abstracted, shared and updated while the useful continuity of meaning must survive those changes. Together they earn a relation neither parent earns alone: when context is locally reconstituted, semantic continuity should be treated like a transition problem rather than raw-state retention—the active representation may change, but the transformation between states must preserve the task-relevant object/meaning.
edges.removal:
without S.sMNy there is no explicit local-frame transformation law grounding coherence under representation change; without S.lul4 there is no task-conditioned lifecycle in which context itself is repeatedly transformed and selected.
Boundary: the relation is structural; context abstraction is not literally a gauge transformation and no group law is asserted for arbitrary memory systems.

edges.title: Local-frame invariance and operation-preserving translation are the same kind of obligation at different substrates
edges.text: S.sMNy supplies covariance: coordinates/components may change while the geometrical operation remains well-defined because transport and kernels obey explicit transformation constraints. S.IIcl supplies cross-paradigm translation that is substantive only when joins, projections, attention, marginalization, message passing and other consumed operations survive the translation. Together they earn an operation-preservation criterion for representation changes: a bridge between representations is trustworthy when the operations required downstream commute with the change of representation closely enough that the same functional object remains addressable.
edges.removal:
without S.sMNy the relation loses an exact transformation-law witness under arbitrary local representation; without S.IIcl it loses a constructive heterogeneous-computation translation witness.
Boundary: this does not claim tensor-logic translations form the same mathematical gauge structure as manifold CNNs.

edges.title: Stable object identity and stable role semantics can coexist without a privileged coordinate realization
edges.text: S.sMNy shows that the same geometrical object may be represented in different local gauges while remaining coherent under an equivariant law. S.6arU shows that content and position keep cleaner semantics when independently meaningful roles occupy separate representational degrees and are joined only at the operation that needs both. Together they derive role-covariant representation: coordinates may change locally without changing what each representational role means, provided the change law preserves those roles and their intended conjunction.
edges.removal:
without S.sMNy there is no witness that coordinate realization may vary while object identity remains; without S.6arU there is no explicit requirement that independently meaningful roles stay independently addressable.
Boundary: the relation does not require every representation to be factorized, only that role distinctions actually required by the task survive representation change.

edges.title: Context portability requires operation-preserving abstraction, not merely compression
edges.text: S.lul4 supplies the lifecycle of summarization, isolation, abstraction, memory layers, retrieval and context selection under minimal sufficiency and semantic continuity. S.IIcl supplies a constructive criterion for useful re-expression: preserve the operative transformations used by downstream inference/learning instead of merely preserving names or approximate surface resemblance. Together they earn a criterion for portable context: summaries, schemas, adapters or shared representations should be judged by whether the operations and dependencies required by the current task remain executable after transformation.
edges.removal:
without S.lul4 there is no long-horizon context lifecycle or minimal-sufficiency pressure; without S.IIcl there is no explicit operation-preserving translation criterion.
Boundary: the source pair does not establish one universal context serialization or compiler.

edges.title: Relevance may change while address semantics remain stable
edges.text: S.lul4 makes context interaction-relative: which memory, tool, dependency or user state is active changes with the current task, and selection must continually decide what deserves to be present. S.6arU shows that an address/position coordinate extrapolates more reliably when its semantics do not silently change with the content occupying it. Together they derive a separation between relevance and address: the set of active context may change aggressively while the semantic meaning of the roles/addresses used to refer to that context remains stable enough for reliable reuse and deliberate conjunction.
edges.removal:
without S.lul4 there is no task-relative changing relevance boundary; without S.6arU there is no empirical architectural witness for stable address semantics under changing content and extended range.
Boundary: not every context system requires geometric positional coordinates; the earned relation is role/address stability under changing active content.

edges.title: A common substrate can preserve independent roles until deliberate conjunction
edges.text: S.IIcl shows that neural, symbolic, kernel and probabilistic computations can inhabit one algebra while retaining the specific operations that make each paradigm distinct. S.6arU shows that content and position can inhabit one attention computation while remaining separately represented until the attention score intentionally combines them. Together they earn a unification discipline: sharing a carrier does not justify collapsing independently meaningful roles; a useful common substrate preserves their operational identity and combines them only at an explicitly named operation.
edges.removal:
without S.IIcl there is no constructive common-substrate unification across heterogeneous computation; without S.6arU there is no direct empirical case where delayed conjunction of independent roles improves behavior.
Boundary: this is not a universal mandate to maximize disentanglement; roles should stay separate only when their independent semantics are load-bearing.

faces.title: Semantic state can move between local representations when the transformation preserves task operations
faces.text: S.sMNy contributes local-frame covariance and explicit transition laws; S.lul4 contributes task-conditioned context transformation over time; S.IIcl contributes operation-preserving re-expression across computational forms. Together they earn a three-way portability criterion: task-relevant semantic state may be summarized, reframed, moved or re-encoded without a privileged global representation when the transformation between local states preserves the operations/dependencies that downstream use actually consumes.
faces.removal: remove S.sMNy and local representation covariance disappears; remove S.lul4 and there is no changing context-state lifecycle; remove S.IIcl and preservation of downstream operations across re-expression is ungrounded.

faces.title: Context can remain coherent without a global canonical frame if local roles keep stable semantics
faces.text: S.sMNy contributes global coherence from overlapping local frames; S.lul4 contributes active reconstitution of context around current relevance; S.6arU contributes stable independent role/address semantics before conjunction. Together they earn noncanonical contextual continuity: a system may maintain different local context views rather than one universal active state, provided the roles used inside those views keep stable semantics and transitions between them preserve what the task needs.
faces.removal: remove S.sMNy and local-view coherence without a global frame disappears; remove S.lul4 and there is no task-relative context view; remove S.6arU and stable independently addressable roles are unearned.

faces.title: Covariant unification preserves both object and role through representation change
faces.text: S.sMNy contributes lawful coordinate change preserving a geometrical object, S.IIcl contributes operation-preserving unification, and S.6arU contributes independent semantic roles with deliberate conjunction. Together they derive covariant factor-preserving unification: a shared representation may change coordinates/substrate while preserving both the whole functional object and the distinct role semantics needed to operate on it.
faces.removal: remove S.sMNy and coordinate-change/object-continuity disappears; remove S.IIcl and there is no operation-preserving cross-form unification; remove S.6arU and role separation before conjunction disappears.

faces.title: Task-conditioned context should expose a stable operational interface even as relevance changes
faces.text: S.lul4 contributes interaction-relative selection and semantic continuity across memory/context layers, S.IIcl contributes executable operation-preserving translation, and S.6arU contributes stable address semantics and independent roles. Together they earn a task-interface criterion: the active context can change with relevance, yet downstream computation should encounter a stable set of role/operation semantics whose meaning is preserved across summaries, memories, adapters or other carriers.
faces.removal: remove S.lul4 and there is no relevance-conditioned changing context; remove S.IIcl and the interface lacks an operation-preserving execution criterion; remove S.6arU and stable independent address/role semantics are unearned.

volume.title: Covariant semantic continuity
volume.text:
Across all four parents, useful identity/meaning repeatedly survives a change of representation without demanding one global canonical realization. S.sMNy shows this formally and architecturally: local gauges may vary while explicit transformation laws preserve a globally well-defined operation. S.lul4 shows that context is not a static blob but a task-conditioned lifecycle in which state is repeatedly collected, summarized, selected, shared, corrected and forgotten while semantic continuity must remain. S.IIcl shows that a common computational language is substantive when translation preserves the operations consumed by inference, learning and composition. S.6arU shows that semantically independent roles remain more reliable when separately addressable until the operation that intentionally combines them.


The complete four-way closure is therefore stronger than “preserve meaning through change.” It specifies what has to be conserved when both context and representation are allowed to vary: the transition between local states must preserve the task-relevant operational object; the active context may change by relevance without redefining stable role/address semantics; translations must preserve the operations actually consumed downstream; and independently meaningful roles must survive until their deliberate conjunction. Under those conditions semantic continuity can live in lawful transformation between local representations rather than in one globally canonical frame, one maximal context snapshot or one fixed carrier.
volume.invariant: Task-relevant meaning can remain stable while both context and representation change when each local rewrite is governed by explicit transition laws that preserve the operations and independent role semantics consumed by the task; semantic continuity then resides in lawful transformation and deliberate conjunction rather than in a privileged global representation or maximal retention of raw state.
removal: Remove S.sMNy: the closure loses the explicit local-frame/covariance witness showing that coordinates may vary while one global operation remains well-defined.
Remove S.lul4: the closure loses the dynamic, relevance-conditioned context lifecycle in which semantic continuity must survive selection, abstraction, update and forgetting.
Remove S.IIcl: the closure loses the constructive criterion that translation must preserve downstream operations across heterogeneous computational representations.
Remove S.6arU: the closure loses the explicit independent-role/address semantics and deliberate-conjunction requirement preventing representation change from smearing distinct obligations together.

metabolites.title: Preserve semantics through explicit transition obligations
metabolites.text: when context or representation is rewritten, continuity should be tested by whether the transition preserves the task-relevant object, operations and dependencies rather than by whether the before/after states look identical.
metabolites.compression: Preserve the obligations across the transition, not the surface form.

metabolites.title: Let relevance change without letting roles change meaning
metabolites.text: task relevance may alter which context is active, but the address/role semantics used to refer to that context should remain stable enough that independent obligations can still be queried and deliberately recombined.
metabolites.compression: Change what is present without changing what each role means.

metabolites.title: Port the operational object, not one canonical representation
metabolites.text: a representation can move across local frames or computational carriers without one canonical global form when transformation laws preserve both the whole operation and the independently meaningful roles it consumes.
metabolites.compression: Port the object by preserving its operations and roles, not by freezing its coordinates.

edges.title: Noncanonical coherence becomes portable only through an operation-preserving interface
edges.text: 1H.hs7W supplies the possibility of coherent function across heterogeneous carriers without one privileged canonical form, plus the requirement that invariance be earned under relevant variation. 1H.qI2L supplies a durable interface whose claim-relevant operations and evidence boundary survive substrate change without asserting shared interior. Together they earn a stricter portability relation: a noncanonical system can expose a stable public correspondence only when the operations that constitute that correspondence are explicitly preserved and the boundary on what it identifies travels with it.
edges.removal:
without 1H.hs7W there is no earned noncanonical/heterogeneous-carrier pressure; without 1H.qI2L there is no operation-preserving public interface or evidence-custody membrane.

volume.title: Evidence-bounded relational portability
volume.text:
Across all four parents, useful continuity repeatedly detaches from fixed internal form, but the complete closure requires more than interface persistence or reconstructibility alone. 1H.hs7W establishes that coherent function can survive noncanonical and heterogeneous carriers only when stable relations, governance and pressure-aligned validation remain explicit. 1H.qI2L establishes that cross-substrate correspondence becomes durable when claim-relevant operations and its evidence boundary are preserved without promoting stable use into shared interior identity. 1H.2VF2 establishes that the needed relation can be dynamically re-instantiated as externally recoverable relational geometry rather than preserved as one element inventory or active snapshot. 1H.9gYl establishes that the portable object should separate semantic obligations, minimize only against an exact downstream task, and earn assurance at the composite rather than inheriting it from trusted parts.


The complete four-way closure is therefore evidence-bounded relational portability: what travels across changing representations, substrates or reconstructed interiors can be an obligation-specific relational kernel rather than a canonical form. That kernel preserves independently meaningful roles, claim-relevant operations, evidence boundaries and only the stable scaffold required to reconstruct the public relation; it deliberately rejoins roles only where the task requires conjunction. Its portability is earned, not assumed: the regenerated relation must survive pressure-aligned carrier/representation variation, external correspondence tests and composite sufficiency checks while remaining explicit about what stable use does not identify.

edges.title: Adaptive reconstruction becomes a typed continuity contract only when every preserved role re-earns composite assurance
edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies a regime-indexed reconstruction/transition family whose scaffold, evidence membrane and admissible rewrites must be re-estimated as conditions move. 2H.Dp9x supplies explicit role-separated obligations and the rule that a reconstructed composite must re-earn end-to-end assurance in the regime where it is used. Together they earn a stricter relation: the transformation family that carries continuity must be typed by the exact operations/roles it promises to preserve, and each reconstructed realization must be tested as a whole rather than inheriting assurance from the map or components.

edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies the locally revisable family of lawful reconstruction and representation transitions. 2H.xqNz supplies the obligation-minimal portable kernel plus pressure-aligned carrier/representation variation designed to expose false invariance. Together they earn a falsifiable portability law: a transition or reconstruction family is admissible only insofar as the regenerated public relation and its evidence membrane survive the relevant variation that should break a merely superficial continuity claim.

edges.title: Continuity has two distinct revision triggers: changed regime and obsolete stabilization
edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies revision when context, representation or local validity regime changes, including revision of the retained scaffold and admissible transformation family. 2H.Dzmx supplies custodial revision when the stabilizing scaffold itself becomes anchor debt and starts preserving the wrong future even if no externally named regime shift has already been recognized. Together they earn dual revision: continuity maintenance must react both to exogenous condition change and to endogenous evidence that its own stabilizing memory has become a source of error.
edges.removal: without 2H.S5EU revision loses the explicit regime/transition dimension; without 2H.Dzmx it loses the endogenous scaffold-debt/obsolescence trigger.

edges.title: A minimal typed reconstruction contract earns portability only through pressure-aligned composite assurance
edges.text: 2H.Dp9x supplies a role-separated reconstruction contract and independent end-to-end assurance in the relevant validity regime. 2H.xqNz supplies minimization to the portable relational kernel and the requirement that invariance survive carrier/representation perturbations while neighboring non-invariants are allowed to move. Together they earn a stronger assurance criterion: a reduced/rebuilt contract is portable only when its exact composite obligation survives relevant variation, not merely when it works in one familiar realization.
edges.removal: without 2H.Dp9x the pressure-tested kernel lacks an explicit role-typed composite obligation; without 2H.xqNz the typed contract lacks the dedicated perturbational witness that earns noncanonical portability.

edges.title: A reconstructible contract must carry an explicit expiry/revision condition

Together they earn an assurance-lifecycle relation: the contract must specify not only what counts as success now, but the evidence or state change under which the current scaffold and assurance cease to be trusted and must be re-earned.
edges.removal: without 2H.Dp9x revision is not tied to an exact composite assurance claim in a witnessed regime; without 2H.Dzmx there is no explicit anchor-debt/expiry condition for the retained scaffold.

edges.title: The portable contract is more stable than any one reconstruction mechanism

Their complete 2H volumes converge on evidence-bounded/reconstructible public contracts despite that change in reconstruction pathway. Together they provide structural substitution evidence: within these selected bodies, the portable obligation/evidence kernel is not tied to one reconstruction mechanism, provided the alternative pathway still regenerates the relation under its pressure and boundary conditions.

volume.title: Reflexive continuity contract
volume.text:
Across all four parents, continuity has already detached from a fixed interior, canonical representation or single reconstruction procedure. The all-four closure adds a higher-order constraint on that freedom. 2H.S5EU makes the admissible reconstruction/transition family and its evidence membrane local to a validity regime and revisable as conditions move. 2H.Dp9x makes the persistent object an explicitly role-typed contract whose reconstructed composite must re-earn end-to-end assurance. 2H.xqNz makes portability a pressure-tested property of an obligation-minimal kernel rather than a consequence of familiar labels or stable parts. 2H.Dzmx adds the second revision channel: the scaffold that once preserved continuity can itself become obsolete anchor debt and must carry the condition of its own retirement or revision.


The complete four-way closure is therefore a reflexive continuity contract: a public relation may remain continuous across changing representations, regimes and reconstruction mechanisms when it is carried as a minimal role-typed contract whose claim-relevant operations and evidence boundary can regenerate the relation, whose transformation/reconstruction family is pressure-tested in the current regime, and whose retained scaffold and map carry explicit revision triggers. The contract is reflexive because part of what it preserves is the information needed to determine when its own continuity claim has stopped being warranted. Continuity is therefore not merely the ability to reproduce a relation; it is the ability to reproduce that relation together with the conditions that can falsify, expire and revise its mode of reproduction.
volume.invariant: A durable public relation can remain continuous across changing representation, regime and reconstruction mechanism when it is carried as a minimal role-typed contract whose claim-relevant operations and evidence boundary can regenerate the relation, whose transition/reconstruction family is pressure-tested within the current regime, and whose scaffold and map include explicit revision triggers when conditions change or prior stabilization becomes bias; continuity is warranted only while the contract preserves both the relation and the conditions for detecting when it no longer does.

Remove 2H.Dp9x: the closure loses explicit role-separated composite obligations and end-to-end reconstruction assurance; the remaining trio can support adaptive, pressure-tested, revisable portability but not the precise typed composite whose continuity is being certified.

Remove 2H.xqNz: the closure loses the independent pressure-aligned carrier-variation witness and obligation-minimal portable-kernel criterion; the remaining trio can describe an adaptive typed self-revising contract but lacks the dedicated stress surface that earns portability under noncanonical variation.

Remove 2H.Dzmx: the closure loses the endogenous anchor-debt/expiry condition and the independent bounded-state reconstruction pathway; the remaining trio can earn regime-typed pressure-tested portability but not the rule that continuity must detect when its own stabilizing scaffold has become the source of invalidity.

metabolites.title: Revise both the map and the memory
metabolites.text: continuity can fail in at least two distinct ways represented here: the environment/representation regime can change so the old transition map is no longer warranted, or the retained scaffold can become an obsolete stabilizing bias even before that change is cleanly named. A living continuity contract therefore needs separate revision paths for map and memory.
metabolites.compression: Revise the map when the world changes; revise the memory when yesterday's stability becomes today's bias.

gaps.title: BOUNDARY UNEXPOSED
gaps.text: No explicit top-level evidence-boundary block was mechanically recognized in this canonical artifact.

edges.title: Context-sensitive validity is a local variable
edges.text: S.dY9d shows that matched changes in opponent/self framing can alter strategic policy, while S.qogS shows that symmetry support or degree may vary by input/equivalence class and disappear inside a global dataset summary. Together they earn a relation neither parent earns alone: when the response law materially changes across local conditions, validity should be represented as condition-indexed structure rather than one global scalar.
edges.removal:
without S.dY9d there is no direct behavioral consequence of a small contextual contrast; without S.qogS there is no explicit local-field formalization or approximation-bounded estimator of heterogeneous validity.
Boundary: this does not imply every system property is local or that global summaries are useless.

edges.title: Functional identity should be witnessed by recurrence across perturbations, not one cue or snapshot
edges.text: S.dY9d limits self-model interpretation by robustness beyond one eliciting phrase/task. S.dgx1 demonstrates pattern identity as repeated restoration of relational constraints across changing visible states, time, damage, and some substrate perturbations. Together they earn a validation rule: an operational identity claim becomes stronger when the target relation recurs under independent perturbations rather than because one label, cue, or activation persists.
edges.removal: without S.dY9d the construct-validity ladder for cue-conditioned identity disappears; without S.dgx1 there is no direct process-identity witness through recurrent reconstruction.

edges.title: Context variables that alter policy are load-bearing constraints in a compressed carrier
edges.text: S.dY9d supplies a contextual variable whose change measurably alters policy. S.boAF supplies a hierarchy in which later local refinement depends on transported coarse constraints and coarse errors propagate. Together they derive that a compressed or hierarchical carrier used to preserve downstream behavior must retain contextual distinctions capable of changing the downstream obligation rather than only an average or aesthetically plausible summary.
edges.removal: without S.dY9d there is no demonstrated policy-changing context distinction; without S.boAF there is no explicit compression/transport mechanism with visible downstream error propagation.

edges.title: Local invariance can be maintained by a recurrent relational process without global uniformity
edges.text: S.qogS supplies input-local symmetry/invariance regimes rather than one global symmetry scalar. S.dgx1 supplies recurrent local dynamics that repeatedly restore relations defining a recognizable pattern. Together they earn a bounded possibility: continuity or invariance may be locally conditioned and dynamically maintained instead of stored as one globally uniform state.
edges.removal:
without S.qogS local heterogeneity of the validity regime disappears; without S.dgx1 dynamic recurrent maintenance disappears.
Boundary: local maintenance is not automatically globally coherent; both parents preserve failure/approximation boundaries.

edges.title: Compression is unsafe when it erases locally heterogeneous structure
edges.text: S.qogS shows that global symmetry summaries can hide input-local support differences; S.boAF shows that coarse hierarchical state can efficiently transport constraints but can also propagate missing or incorrect information into fine detail. Together they earn a sufficiency criterion: a coarse or compressed summary is valid only when it preserves the locally varying distinctions needed by downstream computation.
edges.removal: without S.qogS there is no explicit local heterogeneity hidden by a global summary; without S.boAF there is no constructive hierarchical compression and propagated-error witness.

edges.title: Global organization can persist through distributed local reconstruction plus hierarchical transport
edges.text: S.dgx1 shows a global pattern maintained by a shared local recurrent process; S.boAF shows high-resolution output produced from sparse local patches coordinated by coarse-to-fine feature and gradient transport. Together they earn a structural recurrence: monolithic co-presence of the whole state is not necessary when local modules can reconstruct or refine the whole from transported relational constraints.
edges.removal:
without S.dgx1 regenerative local process identity disappears; without S.boAF explicit sparse hierarchical transport and coarse-to-fine dependency disappear.
Boundary: neither parent establishes that arbitrary local decompositions preserve global function.

faces.title: Operational identity is a context-local recurrent relation
faces.text: S.dY9d contributes context-sensitive strategic self-positioning and a robustness boundary, S.qogS contributes condition-local validity rather than one global scalar, and S.dgx1 contributes identity as recurrent relational reconstruction. Together they earn a three-way criterion: an operational identity or behavioral continuity claim should be indexed to the local condition regime in which it is valid and promoted only to the level at which the same functional relation recurs under independent perturbation.
faces.removal: remove S.dY9d and the identity/behavior claim plus cue-sensitivity boundary disappears; remove S.qogS and locality of the validity regime disappears; remove S.dgx1 and recurrent-process continuity disappears.

faces.title: Diagnostic compression must preserve variables that resolve local behavioral regimes
faces.text: S.dY9d shows a small framing variable that changes policy, S.qogS shows distinct local regimes that can be hidden by a global summary, and S.boAF shows how a hierarchy can compress and transport only selected constraints. Together they earn a diagnostic sufficiency law: a compressed context or representation is adequate only if it retains the locally load-bearing variables that distinguish downstream response regimes.
faces.removal: remove S.dY9d and there is no consequential response variable; remove S.qogS and no locally heterogeneous validity surface; remove S.boAF and no concrete compression/transport architecture or propagation failure.

faces.title: Regenerative compression needs consequential context custody
faces.text: S.dY9d establishes that some context distinctions alter policy, S.dgx1 establishes that recognizable function can be rebuilt from recurrent local state instead of a full history/snapshot, and S.boAF establishes that a hierarchy can transport sufficient constraints through sparse parts. Together they earn a stronger condition for regenerative systems: function may be preserved from partial or reconstructed state only when policy-changing context is carried through the regeneration path and tested for failure.
faces.removal: remove S.dY9d and consequential context disappears; remove S.dgx1 and regeneration from local recurrent state disappears; remove S.boAF and hierarchical sparse custody/transport disappears.

faces.title: Nonuniform local structure can support a coherent whole without one global representation
faces.text: S.qogS contributes local structural regimes, S.dgx1 contributes recurrent local relational process, and S.boAF contributes hierarchical sparse transport. Together they earn a possibility stronger than any pair: a coherent global function can be supported by locally different constraint regimes and distributed reconstruction when local operator semantics and cross-scale dependencies remain intact; failures propagate when those membranes are wrong.
faces.removal: remove S.qogS and local regime heterogeneity disappears; remove S.dgx1 and regenerative local process disappears; remove S.boAF and the explicit global-through-hierarchy transport relation disappears.

volume.title: Regenerative continuity under local validity
volume.text:
Across all four parents, the system need not preserve one globally uniform or fully co-present state. S.dY9d shows that small contextual/self-similarity changes can alter policy and therefore cannot be dismissed as irrelevant metadata when the downstream obligation depends on them. S.qogS shows that structural validity itself may be input-local and approximation-bounded rather than one dataset-wide fact. S.dgx1 shows that recognizable identity/function can persist as a relation repeatedly reconstructed by local recurrent dynamics instead of one static snapshot. S.boAF shows that a sparse hierarchy can transport enough global constraint for later local refinement, while exposing how missing coarse information propagates into downstream failure.


The complete four-way closure is therefore regenerative continuity under local validity: continuity through compressed, sparse, or reconstructed state is earned only relative to a context/input validity regime. The carrier need not preserve the entire interior, but it must preserve every local distinction whose change can alter the downstream obligation, together with enough relational structure to reconstruct that obligation. When the local regime changes, the scaffold or summary must be re-estimated and revalidated rather than treated as a globally invariant identity.
volume.invariant: A distributed system can preserve task-relevant continuity without retaining one complete or globally uniform state when local or hierarchical carriers preserve enough relational structure to reconstruct the required function; that sufficiency is itself context- and input-dependent, so every distinction capable of changing downstream behavior must remain in the carrier or its validity witness, and the reconstruction must be re-estimated when the local regime changes.
removal: Remove S.dY9d: the closure loses direct evidence that a small contextual/self-similarity distinction can change downstream policy, so task-relevant compression lacks a consequential contrast.
Remove S.qogS: the closure loses the local-field and identifiability membrane; the remaining trio can discuss reconstruction under compression but cannot earn locality of validity.
Remove S.dgx1: the closure loses recurrent process identity and reconstruction; hierarchy and conditional validity remain, but regenerative continuity is unearned.

Remove S.boAF: the closure loses explicit sparse hierarchical constraint transport and failure propagation; the remaining trio lacks a concrete compression architecture linking local validity to reduced state.

metabolites.title: Validity can be a field over conditions, not one number for the whole system
metabolites.text: when a system property changes across matched context or input regimes, its validity should be represented as a local field or conditioned relation rather than one global scalar.
metabolites.compression: Validity can be a field over conditions, not one number for the whole system.

metabolites.title: Keep the distinctions that can change the obligation
metabolites.text: a compressed or hierarchical carrier is sufficient only if it preserves the locally varying context and structure whose change can alter downstream behavior; otherwise compression silently collapses distinct operating regimes.
metabolites.compression: Compress aggressively only after proving the distinctions you dropped cannot change the obligation.

metabolites.title: Continuity is a relation that survives revalidation
metabolites.text: a functional identity or continuity claim is stronger when the same relation is repeatedly reconstructed across independent cue, context, and substrate perturbations, with its local validity regime re-estimated rather than presumed fixed.
metabolites.compression: Continuity is a relation that survives revalidation, not a label carried through changing conditions.

gaps.title: BOUNDARY UNEXPOSED
gaps.text: No explicit top-level evidence-boundary block was mechanically recognized in this canonical artifact.

edges.title: Invariance is a lossy quotient whose erased distinctions must be justified
edges.text: S.u1gk supplies the demonstrated consequence that a correct target symmetry can coexist with predictive distributional asymmetry that a hard symmetry-aware learner discards. S.exnj supplies the formal semantics that invariance/sameness is created by declaring a transformation quotient and that broader nuisance groups deliberately erase more distinctions. Together they earn a stricter relation: an invariance declaration is not neutral compression; it is a quotient that removes information, and its legitimacy depends on whether the removed degrees are actually nuisance for the stated obligation.
edges.removal:
without S.u1gk, quotienting lacks evidence that erased non-invariant structure can change downstream risk; without S.exnj, there is no explicit equivalence/quotient contract defining what is being erased.
Boundary: neither parent establishes one universally correct quotient or a universal preference for less invariance.

edges.title: Symmetry scope is locally conditional rather than one dataset-wide policy
edges.text: S.u1gk shows that global distributional symmetry breaking does not determine whether equivariance helps and that task relevance/locality/regime matter. S.qogS supplies a constructive input-dependent symmetry field in which different examples can inhabit different transformation supports. Together they earn that the scope of a symmetry constraint may need to be conditioned on local/task context rather than inferred from one global statistic or one target-level group statement.
edges.removal:
without S.u1gk there is no downstream governance consequence of mismatched symmetry scope; without S.qogS there is no explicit local/input-conditioned symmetry object.
Boundary: the local estimator is assumption-bounded and is not itself an architecture-routing oracle.

edges.title: Preserve independently meaningful factors before deciding what may be quotiented away
edges.text: S.u1gk shows that an apparently non-invariant degree can remain predictive under the encountered distribution and that hard invariance may remove it. S.6arU shows that two necessary factors can remain independently addressable until their deliberate conjunction, avoiding cross-talk without forbidding interaction. Together they earn a protective rule: before treating variation as nuisance, keep independently meaningful factors separately addressable long enough to test whether each affects the task; quotient only after the intended irrelevance has survived a discriminating intervention.
edges.removal:
without S.u1gk there is no evidence that discarded asymmetry may be task-useful; without S.6arU there is no constructive independent-addressability-before-conjunction discipline.
Boundary: independent addressability is a diagnostic/architectural strategy, not proof that all factors should remain permanently separate.

edges.title: More flexible equivalence requires more evidence about where equivalence actually holds
edges.text: S.exnj shows that broader transformation quotients create a finite-sample estimation burden and can erase claim-relevant structure. S.qogS shows that the transformation support itself may vary locally and that local estimates pass through an approximation membrane whose quality depends on neighborhood density, representation and family assumptions. Together they earn an evidence-budget law: increasing invariance flexibility or making equivalence context-sensitive increases the burden of establishing which transformations are genuinely admissible at each relevant locus.
edges.removal:
without S.exnj there is no controlled quotient-flexibility/estimation-cost relation; without S.qogS there is no local identifiability/approximation burden.
Boundary: this is not a universal sample-complexity theorem.

edges.title: Quotient nuisance coordinates without quotienting away the task’s independent roles
edges.text: S.exnj supplies architecture/claim-aware quotienting: admissible transformations must preserve the structure named by the comparison claim. S.6arU supplies a concrete case where content and position remain separate semantic roles until attention deliberately combines them. Together they earn that a valid invariance should erase coordinate realization while preserving the role axes the downstream operation must still query independently.
edges.removal:
without S.exnj there is no explicit nuisance-group/equivalence semantics; without S.6arU there is no independent-role witness showing how a shared operation can combine factors without collapsing their meanings.
Boundary: the correct preserved axes are obligation-specific and must be earned rather than named by analogy.

edges.title: Local transformation support can vary while coordinate roles remain stable
edges.text: S.qogS supplies input-conditioned symmetry support that can change across examples or regimes. S.6arU supplies stable coordinate semantics whose meaning remains fixed while content and range change. Together they earn a compatibility condition for context-sensitive invariance: the set of transformations treated as locally admissible may vary, but the semantic roles used to state and query that variation must remain stable enough that changing support is not confused with changing meaning.
edges.removal:
without S.qogS there is no local variation in admissible symmetry support; without S.6arU there is no explicit stable-role/address semantics under changing regime.
Boundary: local support and coordinate roles are distinct objects; this does not imply one common mathematical mechanism across the two sources.

faces.title: Locally warranted equivalence requires task consequence, quotient semantics and local scope
faces.text: S.u1gk contributes the downstream consequence of discarding task-relevant asymmetry; S.exnj contributes explicit quotient-relative sameness and the cost of broad invariance; S.qogS contributes a locally varying symmetry field and its identification boundary. Together they earn that a transformation may count as nuisance only under a locally warranted equivalence contract: the quotient must be declared, its erased distinctions must be irrelevant to the current task obligation, and the local support on which that claim is made must be sufficiently identified.
faces.removal: remove S.u1gk and irrelevance has no demonstrated task consequence; remove S.exnj and the equivalence relation itself is undefined; remove S.qogS and the scope collapses back toward one global regime.

faces.title: Loss-aware quotienting preserves task-relevant factors until irrelevance is tested
faces.text: S.u1gk contributes evidence that hard symmetry can remove predictive information; S.exnj contributes the formal quotient that determines which distinctions disappear; S.6arU contributes independent addressability and deliberate conjunction. Together they earn a construction discipline: preserve candidate task factors as independently queryable degrees, test their relevance, and only then place truly nuisance variation inside the quotient. A convenient alignment or correct target symmetry is insufficient by itself.
faces.removal: remove S.u1gk and information-loss consequence disappears; remove S.exnj and there is no explicit quotient boundary; remove S.6arU and there is no constructive preserve-before-conjunction strategy.

faces.title: Constraint scope can vary locally without entangling the roles the task must still query
faces.text: S.u1gk contributes task/regime-dependent consequences of symmetry constraints; S.qogS contributes input-local transformation support; S.6arU contributes stable independent role coordinates. Together they earn that an adaptive symmetry policy must vary the admissible transformation scope separately from the semantic roles used by the task. Local changes in invariance must not silently redefine the factors whose conjunction produces the answer.
faces.removal: remove S.u1gk and local scope lacks a task-risk governance reason; remove S.qogS and there is no input-conditioned support; remove S.6arU and local scope can become entangled with task-factor semantics.

faces.title: Context-conditioned quotient continuity has an explicit evidence membrane
faces.text: S.exnj contributes quotient-relative sameness and estimation burden; S.qogS contributes a locally estimated symmetry support with approximation limits; S.6arU contributes stable address semantics under extrapolative change. Together they earn that a context-conditioned equivalence relation can remain interpretable across changing inputs only when the transformation family, its estimation/identification assumptions, and the semantic coordinate roles are carried together. Otherwise a changing quotient is indistinguishable from a changing definition of the object itself.
faces.removal: remove S.exnj and sameness lacks quotient semantics; remove S.qogS and the quotient has no local/context-varying support; remove S.6arU and no stable role/address semantics remain through the scope change.

volume.title: Locally warranted equivalence
volume.text:
Across all four parents, invariance becomes a governed, evidence-bearing operation rather than an intrinsic property that can be imposed globally without cost. S.u1gk separates target symmetry, encountered distribution symmetry and learner-imposed symmetry and demonstrates that erasing non-invariant structure can change risk. S.exnj makes representational sameness explicitly quotient-relative and shows that broader invariance both erases more structure and raises estimation burden. S.qogS makes the admissible symmetry regime itself local/input-dependent and preserves the approximation boundary on identifying that regime. S.6arU shows how task factors can remain independently addressable with stable semantics until an intentional conjunction, preventing a representational convenience from silently rewriting the roles a task needs.


The complete four-way closure is therefore: equivalence/invariance should be treated as a locally warranted, task-conditioned quotient rather than a global declaration of sameness. A transformation may be ignored only where current evidence supports that the distinction it erases is nuisance for the present obligation. Independently meaningful task factors should remain separately addressable until that irrelevance is tested and the intended conjunction occurs. Because admissible symmetry/equivalence scope can vary across inputs and regimes, and broader quotients create both information-loss and estimation debt, the quotient must carry its local validity/identifiability boundary and be re-evaluated when context changes.
volume.invariant: A system can preserve useful equivalence across changing representations by quotienting only transformations that are locally warranted as nuisance for the current task, while keeping independently meaningful factors separately addressable until deliberate conjunction; the transformation scope and its evidence boundary must travel together because local symmetry can vary and broader invariance can erase predictive structure or exceed the evidence available to identify the equivalence.
removal: Remove S.u1gk: the closure loses the demonstrated distinction among target, data and imposed symmetry and the evidence that an incorrect hard quotient can delete predictive information.
Remove S.exnj: the closure loses explicit quotient-relative sameness, metric/equivalence semantics and the evidence cost of widening nuisance freedom.
Remove S.qogS: the closure loses the input-local symmetry field and the approximation/identifiability membrane that makes transformation scope context-dependent.

Remove S.6arU: the closure loses the constructive rule that independently meaningful roles can remain separately addressable with stable semantics until deliberate conjunction.


DERIVED CROSS-ORGANISM INVARIANTS


INV-1H.F8cX-LOCAL-QUOTIENT — Treat invariance as a locally warranted equivalence contract
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:wxy
Invariant: A transformation should count as nuisance only after an explicit quotient is declared, the erased distinction is shown to be irrelevant to the stated task obligation, and the local/contextual support on which that equivalence is asserted is sufficiently identified.
CREATE: state the task obligation, candidate nuisance transformation family, and local regime in which equivalence is proposed.
COPY: carry the same quotient definition together with its task/local validity conditions when reusing the comparison or constraint.
CONTROL: reject global or target-only symmetry claims as sufficient authorization for hard invariance when local/task evidence disagrees or remains unidentified.
CULTIVATE: re-estimate the admissible transformation support as data distribution, context, model regime or task changes.
Compression: equivalence is warranted locally; it is not free global sameness.


INV-1H.F8cX-PRESERVE-BEFORE-QUOTIENT — Preserve candidate task factors until nuisance status survives intervention
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:wxz
Invariant: Before quotienting a variable or transformation away, keep the potentially independent factor addressable long enough to test whether its variation carries task-relevant information; only distinctions that survive that relevance test as nuisance should be erased.
CREATE: separate candidate semantic/task factors from candidate nuisance coordinates.
COPY: preserve those roles independently through representation and evaluation so changing one does not silently rewrite another.
CONTROL: independently vary the candidate factors and transformations; block quotienting when the supposedly nuisance degree changes the required outcome or evidential claim.
CULTIVATE: introduce deliberate conjunction only after role independence and nuisance irrelevance have been stress-tested across broader regimes.
Compression: test a distinction before making it disappear.


INV-1H.F8cX-EVIDENCE-BUDGET — Invariance flexibility cannot outrun equivalence identification
Minimal body: 1H.F8cX:xy
Invariant: More permissive or more context-sensitive equivalence increases the burden of identifying the admissible transformation set and estimating stable comparisons; invariance scope should expand only as evidence supports the additional nuisance freedom.
CREATE: pair every proposed quotient/symmetry-support family with an explicit estimation and identification regime.
COPY: preserve sample density, alignment/estimator family, neighborhood assumptions and validation protocol with the equivalence claim.
CONTROL: test convergence, neighborhood fidelity and counter-transformations that should remain visible; treat unstable local estimates or over-flexible alignment as open identification debt.
CULTIVATE: widen or localize the quotient incrementally as additional evidence closes the corresponding estimation burden.
Compression: every additional ignored degree of freedom must be paid for with evidence.


METABOLITE-COLLAPSE PASS
A candidate “use local symmetry instead of global symmetry” metabolite was rejected as too broad: S.qogS does not establish universal local identifiability and S.u1gk does not show that local constraints always dominate global ones. A candidate “disentanglement is always better” metabolite was rejected because S.6arU explicitly preserves deliberate conjunction and the other parents only require distinctions relevant to the present claim. A candidate “more invariance is worse” metabolite was rejected because S.u1gk contains regimes where symmetrization helps and S.exnj treats broader quotienting as a legitimate choice with an evidence cost rather than a universal error. Three metabolites survive collapse: locally warranted quotient scope, preserve-before-quotient intervention, and the evidence budget of invariance flexibility.

metabolites.compression: equivalence is warranted locally; it is not free global sameness.
