1H.DUwl.title: revalidatable operational continuity
1H.DUwl.boundary:
This child is a cross-source relational synthesis, not evidence that the four source domains share one mechanism.
S.IIcl contributes a formal/constructive language claim about operation-preserving translation and executable tensor programs.
S.fGb4 contributes benchmark-bounded empirical evidence about compact video-history carriers, query coverage, downstream repurposing, anisotropic information loss, and modular memory extensions; its separately referenced supplement remains outside the chosen carrier.
S.fOgn contributes empirical held-out intracranial neural-encoding evidence from four clinical participants and preserves the explicit boundary that predictive coordinate alignment does not establish code, mechanism, architecture, or causal-pathway identity; separate supplementary material remains outside the chosen carrier.
S.CTLJ contributes a conceptual/literature-grounded design argument about autonomy, multiscale coordination, continuous rebuilding, embodiment, signaling, and cognitive-light-cone expansion; it does not experimentally establish necessity, sufficiency, AGI, or consciousness.
All claims below remain bounded by those source evidence classes.

edges.title: operation-bounded compression
edges.text: Holding S.IIcl with S.fGb4 yields a criterion stronger than either alone: a compact carrier is useful for continuity when its reduction preserves or can re-expose the task-relevant operations that later computation actually needs, while its scarce capacity remains repurposable as the task changes. S.IIcl supplies the operation-preserving translation criterion; S.fGb4 supplies empirical finite-capacity compression, unpredictable-access training, downstream adaptation, and ablations showing selective loss.
edges.removal: without S.IIcl, compression lacks an explicit cross-representation criterion for what operational structure must survive; without S.fGb4, the relation lacks a concrete bounded-memory regime demonstrating that broad access and later repurposing compete for selective capacity.

edges.title: correspondence without identity
edges.text: Holding S.IIcl with S.fOgn yields an explicit distinction between useful representational correspondence and ontological identity. A mapping can preserve enough operations or predictive geometry to support cross-representation work even when the systems being related have different mechanisms, architectures, or internal codes. S.IIcl supplies constructive operation-preserving translation; S.fOgn supplies held-out empirical alignment plus an explicit alternative in which a learned map relates distinct biological and model codes.
edges.removal: without S.IIcl there is no formal account of how translation can remain computationally substantive; without S.fOgn there is no empirical cross-system case forcing the non-identity boundary to remain live.

edges.title: reconstructible operational contract
edges.text: Holding S.IIcl with S.CTLJ yields a carrier-independent continuity principle: if the operations and relations that define current competence are explicit enough to be re-instantiated, the implementation carrying them may be rebuilt without treating bytewise or architectural sameness as identity. S.IIcl supplies the addressable operational program/translation structure; S.CTLJ supplies continual reconstruction, self-maintained goals, and multiscale coordination as the system-level reason to permit implementation turnover.
edges.removal: without S.IIcl the reconstruction criterion lacks an explicit operational interface; without S.CTLJ the relation lacks the system-level developmental claim that continuing competence may require rebuilding its own carrier.

edges.title: downstream-warranted latent sufficiency
edges.text: Holding S.fGb4 with S.fOgn yields a shared empirical lesson across unrelated domains: a reduced or learned latent representation should be judged by held-out downstream usefulness under its stated task and evidence regime, not by exhaustive recovery of source detail or by assuming that predictive similarity identifies the generating mechanism. TinyHistory tests future-generation continuity under compression; the neural study tests held-out biological predictivity while retaining a code/mechanism gap.
edges.removal: without S.fGb4 there is no finite-memory repurposing/compression stress surface; without S.fOgn there is no independent ecological predictive case that makes non-identity an explicit part of the warrant.

edges.title: goal-conditioned repurposing
edges.text: Holding S.fGb4 with S.CTLJ yields a developmental relation: a memory/carrier may remain continuous by changing what it allocates capacity to, provided repurposing is governed by the goals and constraints that define current competent behavior rather than by preservation of every prior feature. TinyHistory supplies the freeze-versus-adapt evidence and selective bottleneck; S.CTLJ supplies the conceptual account of protected goals, reconstructive identity, and changing problem horizons.
edges.removal: without S.fGb4 the relation lacks empirical evidence that a broadly useful pretrained carrier must be reshaped for downstream continuity; without S.CTLJ the reshaping lacks a system-level continuity criterion beyond the local training objective.

edges.title: action-usable coordinates with an ontology boundary
edges.text: Holding S.fOgn with S.CTLJ yields a bounded account of internal models/coordinates: a coarse learned representation can be useful for prediction and potentially action without being a veridical copy or the same mechanism as the system it predicts. S.fOgn shows a concrete predictive coordinate relation that survives held-out natural data while leaving mechanism identity unsettled; S.CTLJ argues that action-guiding models need only be sufficiently informative for maintained goals and may remain coarse-grained.
edges.removal: without S.fOgn the claim lacks a concrete cross-system predictive witness and explicit ontology fork; without S.CTLJ it lacks the goal-directed reason that a non-identical coordinate system can still be functionally sufficient.

faces.title: task-warranted operational representation
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fGb4 + S.fOgn jointly earn a stronger notion of representational sufficiency: the relevant carrier must preserve executable/task-relevant relations across representation change, survive finite-capacity selection and downstream repurposing, and be validated against held-out behavior while its map is not promoted into mechanism identity. Remove S.IIcl and “sufficiency” loses the operation-preserving translation criterion; remove S.fGb4 and it loses the concrete compression/repurposing stress; remove S.fOgn and it loses independent held-out cross-system validation plus the explicit non-identity boundary.

faces.title: reconstructible operational memory
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fGb4 + S.CTLJ jointly earn a memory/competence carrier that can change its implementation while remaining continuous: an explicit operational interface states what must remain executable, a compact carrier demonstrates that scarce representational capacity can be repurposed rather than frozen, and a reconstructive goal-directed system supplies the continuity criterion for when such reorganization is still the same competence. Remove S.IIcl and there is no explicit operational contract; remove S.fGb4 and there is no bounded empirical repurposing witness; remove S.CTLJ and there is no system-level reconstruction/goal continuity condition.

faces.title: non-identical coordinate governance
faces.text: S.IIcl + S.fOgn + S.CTLJ jointly earn a way to coordinate across heterogeneous representations without collapsing them ontologically: relations may be translated into an operation-preserving public interface, predictive coordinate maps may remain useful while internal mechanisms differ, and higher-level goals/constraints may govern which relations must remain available as implementation changes. Remove S.IIcl and the public relation lacks a constructive translation criterion; remove S.fOgn and the non-identity boundary loses its empirical cross-system witness; remove S.CTLJ and the relation loses the goal/constraint layer that governs reconstruction and multiscale use.

faces.title: revalidatable sufficiency under drift
faces.text: S.fGb4 + S.fOgn + S.CTLJ jointly earn a dynamic criterion for “enough representation”: the carrier may be compressed and repurposed, but sufficiency must be re-tested on held-out downstream behavior and reconsidered when the task, goal, or problem horizon changes; predictive usefulness never by itself proves mechanism identity. Remove S.fGb4 and the criterion loses finite-capacity repurposing and selective information-loss evidence; remove S.fOgn and it loses independent held-out ecological validation plus the ontology boundary; remove S.CTLJ and it loses the explicit system-level reason that the validation regime itself may have to change as competence expands.

volume.title: revalidatable operational continuity
volume.text:
All four parents together earn the following bounded closure:


A changing system can preserve task-relevant continuity without preserving a fixed implementation or exhaustive archive when it carries a compact, explicitly operational interface whose transformations preserve the relations needed for current computation; keeps that carrier repurposable under finite capacity as downstream demands change; revalidates adequacy against held-out behavior while preserving the distinction between useful correspondence and mechanism identity; and lets maintained goals, constraints, and an expanding problem horizon determine when the interface or its realization must be reconstructed again. Continuity is therefore warranted by re-executable relation plus renewed evidence, not by material sameness, total retention, or representational resemblance alone.


Full-rank removal tests:
- Remove S.IIcl: the volume loses the explicit operation-preserving translation/executability criterion and falls back to task-specific predictive usefulness.
- Remove S.fGb4: the volume loses direct evidence that finite-capacity carriers require selective access pressure, downstream repurposing, and trade-offs in what survives.
- Remove S.fOgn: the volume loses independent held-out cross-system validation and the explicit proof barrier between predictive correspondence and mechanism/code identity.
- Remove S.CTLJ: the volume loses the system-level goal, reconstruction, and expanding-horizon condition that explains when a once-sufficient carrier must be rebuilt or revalidated.


Bounded volume invariant:
Continuity through changing realization is earned when a compact operational relation can be regenerated for the current task, its adequacy is externally revalidated under the current evidence regime, and the conditions that trigger repurposing or reconstruction travel with the relation; neither implementation sameness nor representational correspondence alone is sufficient.

metabolites.title: OPERATIONAL-SUFFICIENCY
metabolites.text: Under bounded capacity, preservation should target the operations and accesses the downstream task must still perform rather than exhaustive source detail.
metabolites.compression: preserve what must still be doable, then test that it remains doable.

metabolites.title: CORRESPONDENCE-WITHOUT-IDENTITY
metabolites.text: A representation-to-representation map can be operationally or predictively useful without establishing that the mapped systems share the same code, mechanism, architecture, or causal process.
metabolites.compression: a real bridge need not make its shores identical.

metabolites.title: GOAL-CONDITIONED-REPURPOSING
metabolites.text: A carrier can remain continuous by reallocating scarce representational capacity when the continuity criterion is expressed by maintained goals and downstream competence rather than by frozen feature preservation.
metabolites.compression: continuity may require changing what memory spends itself on.

metabolites.title: REVALIDATABLE-RECONSTRUCTION
metabolites.text: Reconstruction counts as continued competence only when the relation to be preserved is operationally explicit, the carrier can be repurposed under finite capacity, adequacy is re-witnessed outside the carrier itself, and goal/regime change can revoke the old warrant.
metabolites.compression: preserve the relation, preserve the test, and preserve the right to revise both.

2H.AvDK.title: regime-revisable reconstructive continuity
2H.AvDK.boundary: This child is a cross-holon relational synthesis over four already-metabolized 1H organisms. It does not promote any parent’s heterogeneous source evidence into one shared mechanism, ontology, or universal law. Every statement below remains bounded by the parent bodies’ existing evidence boundaries. In particular, “continuity,” “identity,” “sufficiency,” “regeneration,” “validity,” and “warrant” are used as operational relational terms earned by the parent bodies, not as evidence of phenomenology, mechanism identity, or substrate-independent metaphysics.

edges.title: custodied operational selectivity
edges.text: Holding 1H.DUwl with 1H.OgQZ yields a stronger criterion for selective state than either earns alone: a system may keep only part of its information actively represented, but that active slice counts as sufficient only when it preserves or can re-expose the operations the present task requires while the larger evidential body remains reacquirable. 1H.DUwl supplies the explicit operational interface and external revalidation criterion; 1H.OgQZ supplies whole-body reachability, selective activation, and evidence custody.
edges.removal: without 1H.DUwl, selective activation lacks a task-explicit criterion for what must remain executable; without 1H.OgQZ, operational sufficiency lacks the reacquirable whole and custody boundary that prevents omitted state from becoming silently deleted evidence.

edges.title: contracted bounded regeneration
edges.text: Holding 1H.DUwl with 1H.L4ld yields an operational account of regenerative continuity: bounded recurrent state can stand in for a complete persistent state only when it can regenerate a stated operational relation and that relation is revalidated outside the scaffold itself. 1H.DUwl supplies the contract and renewed test; 1H.L4ld supplies bounded recurrent reconstruction and the fact that a stabilizing scaffold can become an obsolete bias.
edges.removal: without 1H.DUwl, regeneration lacks an explicit task relation and external adequacy criterion; without 1H.L4ld, the relation lacks a concrete bounded-state reconstruction principle and the anchor-debt condition that motivates scaffold revision.

edges.title: condition-indexed operational warrant
edges.text: Holding 1H.DUwl with 1H.8KP9 makes the warrant for operational continuity explicitly conditional. A relation may remain executable and empirically adequate in one regime without being globally sufficient; therefore the evidence regime, context variables that can alter the downstream obligation, and reconstruction/revalidation triggers must travel with the operational contract. 1H.DUwl supplies re-executable relation plus renewed evidence; 1H.8KP9 supplies local validity and the requirement to preserve consequential distinctions.
edges.removal: without 1H.DUwl, local validity is not tied to an explicit operational relation that can be re-tested; without 1H.8KP9, revalidation lacks a condition-indexed membrane and may incorrectly promote a locally sufficient interface into a global one.

edges.title: reacquirable scaffolded continuity
edges.text: Holding 1H.OgQZ with 1H.L4ld yields a separation between dormant whole, active scaffold, and reconstructed function. The larger body may remain addressable rather than simultaneously active, while bounded state repeatedly re-instantiates the current relation; however, the very scaffold that makes this cheap can bias which futures remain reachable and therefore must stay revisable. 1H.OgQZ supplies dormant-but-reacquirable evidence and selective work; 1H.L4ld supplies recurrent reconstruction and anchor debt.
edges.removal: without 1H.OgQZ, bounded regeneration has no guarantee that inactive source/evidence remains recoverable; without 1H.L4ld, selective reachability has no recurrent mechanism explaining how a small active state can reconstruct continued function or when its stabilizer becomes a liability.

edges.title: locally custodied selectivity
edges.text: Holding 1H.OgQZ with 1H.8KP9 yields a stronger rule for selective processing: omission from active computation is lawful only when locally consequential context and claim/evidence boundaries remain either carried by the active state or exactly reacquirable. A compressed active view must not collapse distinct response regimes merely because the omitted material is currently dormant. 1H.OgQZ supplies selective activation with source custody; 1H.8KP9 supplies local validity and sufficiency-preserving compression.
edges.removal: without 1H.OgQZ, local-regime preservation lacks a whole-body reacquisition/custody discipline; without 1H.8KP9, selective custody lacks a criterion for which dormant distinctions are load-bearing for the current downstream obligation.

edges.title: regime-triggered scaffold revision
edges.text: Holding 1H.L4ld with 1H.8KP9 yields a revision law for regenerative state: a scaffold is a legitimate continuity carrier only within the conditions under which it still reconstructs the target relation, and it must be re-estimated when the local regime moves or when its stabilizing bias blocks required change. 1H.L4ld supplies bounded reconstruction plus anchor debt; 1H.8KP9 supplies condition-local validity and re-estimation.
edges.removal: without 1H.L4ld, regime change has no bounded regenerative scaffold whose bias can be revised; without 1H.8KP9, scaffold revision lacks a condition-indexed validity surface and risks treating one successful recurrent regime as globally stable.

faces.title: selective reconstructive contract
faces.text: 1H.DUwl + 1H.OgQZ + 1H.L4ld jointly earn a compact continuity architecture: state may be selectively active and bounded, the larger evidential whole may remain dormant but reacquirable, and the active scaffold may regenerate the current relation, provided that relation is operationally explicit and externally revalidated.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and the architecture loses an explicit operational/revalidation contract; remove 1H.OgQZ and it loses reacquirable whole-body custody under selectivity; remove 1H.L4ld and it loses bounded recurrent reconstruction plus the scaffold-bias revision pressure.

faces.title: regime-typed selective sufficiency
faces.text: 1H.DUwl + 1H.OgQZ + 1H.8KP9 jointly earn an evidence-bounded notion of “enough active state”: the active carrier must preserve or re-expose the operations currently required, the larger source/evidence body must remain reacquirable, and the sufficiency claim must name the local regime and consequential distinctions under which it was tested.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and sufficiency loses the operational task criterion; remove 1H.OgQZ and it loses selective custody and reacquirable whole-body evidence; remove 1H.8KP9 and it loses regime typing plus the protection against collapsing locally distinct obligations.

faces.title: revalidatable regenerative scaffold
faces.text: 1H.DUwl + 1H.L4ld + 1H.8KP9 jointly earn a scaffold whose right to stand for continued function is neither permanent nor purely internal: it must regenerate an explicit operational relation, be revalidated under the current evidence regime, and be revised or re-estimated when local conditions change or the scaffold’s old stabilizing role becomes bias.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and the scaffold loses an external operational criterion; remove 1H.L4ld and there is no bounded recurrent scaffold/anchor debt to regulate; remove 1H.8KP9 and the validity/revision surface loses local condition typing.

faces.title: custodied adaptive regeneration
faces.text: 1H.OgQZ + 1H.L4ld + 1H.8KP9 jointly earn adaptive reconstruction without global co-presence: the whole remains reacquirable, bounded state regenerates only what is currently needed, and local validity determines which contextual distinctions must be carried or reopened; scaffold bias and regime change can both force renewed reconstruction.
faces.removal: remove 1H.OgQZ and adaptive regeneration loses exact whole/evidence reacquisition under selective activation; remove 1H.L4ld and it loses the bounded recurrent mechanism plus anchor-debt diagnosis; remove 1H.8KP9 and it loses the local validity surface that tells the system when omitted distinctions or stale scaffolds have become consequential.

volume.title: regime-revisable reconstructive continuity
volume.text:
All four parents together earn a continuity warrant that is itself part of the state that must survive and change. 1H.DUwl makes the preserved relation operationally explicit and externally revalidatable. 1H.OgQZ permits only part of the whole to remain actively represented while keeping the larger evidence/source body reacquirable and claim boundaries in custody. 1H.L4ld shows how bounded recurrent state can regenerate function while exposing the debt created by stabilizing scaffolds. 1H.8KP9 makes sufficiency conditional on the local regime and requires consequential distinctions to survive or be re-estimated when conditions change.


The complete closure is therefore regime-revisable reconstructive continuity: task-relevant continuity through changing internal realization is warranted when a bounded scaffold can regenerate an explicitly stated operational relation from selectively active state while the larger evidential body remains reacquirable; the carrier preserves every condition known to alter the downstream obligation; and both the scaffold and its sufficiency warrant are re-estimated when task, regime, or stabilizing bias changes. Selective compression may reduce active burden, but it cannot erase the evidence or contextual distinctions needed to detect that the old continuity warrant has expired.
volume.invariant: A reconstruction can count as continued task-relevant function only when its operational obligation, reacquirable evidence boundary, bounded regenerative scaffold, and local validity regime remain jointly addressable and revisable; the continuity warrant itself must travel with the reconstructed state, because a system that cannot detect when its regime or scaffold has become insufficient cannot lawfully claim that regeneration preserved the same function.
removal: Remove 1H.DUwl: the closure loses the explicit operational relation and external revalidation criterion; what remains can adaptively reconstruct state but cannot state precisely what functional continuity must still do.

Remove 1H.OgQZ: the closure loses whole-body reacquisition and selective evidence custody; a compact scaffold may still be revised and revalidated, but omitted evidence can silently disappear from the continuity claim.

Remove 1H.L4ld: the closure loses the bounded recurrent scaffold and anchor-debt mechanism; what remains can type and test a selective interface but does not earn regeneration from bounded state or diagnose stabilization as a future constraint.

Remove 1H.8KP9: the closure loses condition-local validity and sufficiency-preserving context; revalidation and scaffold revision remain possible, but the claim can no longer earn the rule that locally different regimes require different continuity warrants.

metabolites.title: CUSTODIED-SUFFICIENCY
metabolites.text: selective state counts as sufficient only when it preserves or can re-expose the operations required now, keeps the larger evidential body reacquirable, and carries the local regime/evidence boundary that limits the sufficiency claim.
metabolites.compression: reduce active burden without reducing the system’s ability to know what the reduction was allowed to forget.

metabolites.title: REVISION-TRIGGERED-RECONSTRUCTION
metabolites.text: a bounded regenerative scaffold remains a continuity carrier only while it reconstructs the explicit target relation inside its witnessed validity regime; scaffold bias or regime shift must be able to revoke that warrant and trigger re-estimation.
metabolites.compression: what enables return must also carry the conditions under which return stops counting as the same function.

metabolites.title: WARRANT-AS-STATE
metabolites.text: the right to call a reconstruction “continued function” is itself living state composed of an operational obligation, an evidence/reacquisition boundary, scaffold assumptions, and a validity regime; that warrant must be preserved, tested, and revised alongside the reconstructed content.
metabolites.compression: preserve not only the relation, but the system’s ability to know why it still counts and when it no longer does.

edges.title: Operational continuity can be carried by regenerated relational geometry
edges.text: 1H.DUwl requires an explicit operation-level obligation plus external revalidation; 1H.2VF2 shows that the carrier of competence may be a relation-generating geometry rather than fixed elements. Together they earn a stronger relation: changing internal realizations may count as one operational continuity when a regenerated relational geometry preserves the task-relevant operations and remains externally recoverable under a declared test surface.
edges.removal:
without 1H.DUwl, recoverable relational geometry has no explicit operation-level adequacy/revalidation criterion; without 1H.2VF2, operational continuity has no constructive relational carrier that can be regenerated across changing realization.
Boundary: external recoverability witnesses usefulness, not shared implementation or ontology.

edges.title: Operational equivalence is local and evidence-typed
edges.text: 1H.DUwl supplies the rule that continuity must be revalidated against current task obligations and may be revoked after repurposing; 1H.F8cX supplies locally warranted quotienting plus an evidence budget for deciding which differences are nuisance. Together they derive that operational equivalence is not a blanket sameness claim: it is a task-local quotient whose admissibility must be revalidated at the strength of evidence available.
edges.removal: without 1H.DUwl, local quotienting lacks a concrete operational adequacy/revocation surface; without 1H.F8cX, revalidation lacks an explicit law for which representational differences may be ignored.

edges.title: Reconstruction contracts must carry consequential context
edges.text: 1H.DUwl supplies a compact operational relation plus explicit reconstruction/revalidation triggers; 1H.8KP9 supplies local validity and the requirement that policy-changing/context-changing distinctions survive compression. Together they earn a context-indexed reconstruction contract: a regenerated interface preserves continuity only while it carries every distinction known to alter the downstream obligation and is revalidated when that local regime changes.
edges.removal: without 1H.DUwl, there is no explicit operational contract or external adequacy witness; without 1H.8KP9, the contract has no law requiring load-bearing context to travel with reconstruction or to be re-estimated by regime.

edges.title: Relational carriers are equivalent only under an explicit quotient
edges.text: 1H.2VF2 supplies relation-generating geometry whose externally relevant structure may survive changed realization; 1H.F8cX supplies the locally warranted quotient distinguishing nuisance transformation from independently meaningful factors. Together they earn quotient-bounded relational portability: two regenerated geometries may count as equivalent for a task only under a declared transformation class whose nuisance status is locally supported, while task-relevant factors remain addressable.
edges.removal: without 1H.2VF2, the quotient has no reconstructive relational carrier to act upon; without 1H.F8cX, relational correspondence can drift into unqualified sameness or erase meaningful factors.

edges.title: Regenerative geometry is valid only inside a witnessed local regime
edges.text: 1H.2VF2 shows that relational geometry can be re-instantiated from changing internal realization and judged by external recoverability; 1H.8KP9 shows that the sufficiency of a compressed/reconstructed carrier is local to context/input conditions and must be re-estimated after regime change. Together they earn locally regenerative geometry: relation-generating reconstruction can preserve function without global co-presence only while the local validity field and load-bearing distinctions needed for external recovery are preserved.
edges.removal: without 1H.2VF2, there is no explicit reconstructive relational geometry; without 1H.8KP9, there is no context-indexed sufficiency membrane or re-estimation requirement.

edges.title: Safe quotienting and safe compression share a local validity witness
edges.text: 1H.F8cX shows that broad invariance can erase predictive factors unless nuisance transformations are locally warranted; 1H.8KP9 shows that compressed/hierarchical carriers fail when locally consequential distinctions are dropped. Together they derive a common validity condition: both quotienting and compression are lawful only when the same local evidence boundary shows that removed distinctions cannot change the downstream obligation, and that boundary must be re-estimated when the regime changes.
edges.removal: without 1H.F8cX, there is no explicit nuisance/equivalence decision or evidence budget; without 1H.8KP9, there is no reconstructive/compression failure witness tying erased distinctions to downstream behavior.

faces.title: Evidence-typed regenerative interface
faces.text: 1H.DUwl contributes an explicit operational obligation plus current revalidation, 1H.2VF2 contributes reconstructive relational geometry, and 1H.F8cX contributes a locally warranted nuisance quotient. Together they earn an interface criterion: a changed realization may substitute for a prior one when it regenerates the task-relevant relation, preserves the declared operation, and differs only along transformations currently evidenced as nuisance; this still does not establish implementation identity.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and there is no operation-level adequacy/revalidation criterion; remove 1H.2VF2 and no regenerative relational carrier remains; remove 1H.F8cX and the equivalence scope becomes unbounded.

faces.title: Reconstructive continuity needs a local witness
faces.text: 1H.DUwl contributes explicit operation and revalidation, 1H.2VF2 contributes relation-generating reconstruction, and 1H.8KP9 contributes locally varying sufficiency plus custody of consequential context. Together they earn a complete reconstructive-continuity witness: changing internal state may regenerate the same task-relevant operation through relational geometry, but only while the context variables needed for the obligation and external recovery remain present and the current regime has been revalidated.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and operational adequacy becomes unspecified; remove 1H.2VF2 and regenerative relational realization disappears; remove 1H.8KP9 and local-regime sufficiency/custody disappears.

faces.title: The continuity warrant is locally revocable
faces.text: 1H.DUwl contributes revocation after task/regime-changing repurposing and external revalidation; 1H.F8cX contributes the evidence-typed local quotient; 1H.8KP9 contributes local validity plus re-estimation when conditions change. Together they earn a higher-order claim: the continuity/equivalence warrant itself is state carried with the interface. It remains valid only inside the current task/regime/evidence envelope and must be revoked, narrowed or regenerated when those conditions cease to support the same quotient and obligation.
faces.removal: remove 1H.DUwl and there is no explicit operational revocation/revalidation contract; remove 1H.F8cX and the equivalence boundary becomes undefined; remove 1H.8KP9 and the warrant loses its context-indexed validity and regime-change trigger.

faces.title: Regime-bounded relational regeneration
faces.text: 1H.2VF2 contributes reconstructive relational geometry and external recoverability; 1H.F8cX contributes local nuisance quotienting and preservation of independently meaningful factors; 1H.8KP9 contributes local validity and load-bearing-context custody. Together they earn a representation law: relational geometry may be regenerated, compressed and quotiented across realizations without one canonical state only where local evidence licenses the ignored transformations and the remaining carrier preserves every distinction required for downstream recovery.
faces.removal: remove 1H.2VF2 and there is no relational regeneration mechanism; remove 1H.F8cX and ignored transformations lack a lawful quotient; remove 1H.8KP9 and local sufficiency/regime re-estimation disappears.

volume.title: Revocable reconstructive continuity
volume.text:
Across all four parents, continuity is neither fixed-state persistence nor unrestricted representational equivalence. 1H.2VF2 supplies a constructive carrier: externally recoverable relational geometry can be regenerated across changing internal realization. 1H.DUwl supplies the obligation and witness: the regenerated relation must preserve explicit task-relevant operations and be externally revalidated, with repurposing able to revoke the old claim. 1H.F8cX supplies the equivalence membrane: only locally evidenced nuisance transformations may be quotiented, and independently meaningful factors must remain addressable until their irrelevance is demonstrated. 1H.8KP9 supplies the local-validity membrane: the compressed or reconstructed carrier must retain distinctions capable of changing downstream behavior and must re-estimate its sufficiency when the regime changes.


The full closure is therefore revocable reconstructive continuity: a system may preserve task-relevant continuity through changing realization by regenerating an externally recoverable relational geometry rather than preserving one canonical state, but the operational obligation, locally warranted quotient, load-bearing context and evidence/validity boundary must travel with the reconstruction. The continuity/equivalence warrant is itself a revocable state: when task, regime, nuisance structure or carrier sufficiency changes, the old warrant must be narrowed, withdrawn or regenerated and revalidated rather than silently inherited.
volume.invariant: Task-relevant continuity across changing realization is warranted when an externally recoverable relational geometry can be regenerated while preserving the declared operation-level obligation, every locally load-bearing distinction, and only quotienting differences whose nuisance status is supported by the current evidence regime; the resulting continuity/equivalence warrant travels as revocable state and must be revalidated or rebuilt whenever task, regime, quotient scope or carrier sufficiency changes.
removal: Remove 1H.DUwl: reconstruction, local validity and quotienting remain, but there is no explicit operation-level obligation, external adequacy test or revocation contract; continuity becomes structurally plausible rather than operationally warranted.

Remove 1H.2VF2: revalidation, quotienting and local validity remain, but the closure loses the positive reconstructive carrier—relation-generating geometry—that explains how continuity can survive changing realization without one fixed state.

Remove 1H.F8cX: reconstruction, operation and local validity remain, but the closure cannot state which differences may lawfully be ignored or how much evidence is required before representational variation counts as equivalent.

Remove 1H.8KP9: reconstruction, operational revalidation and local quotienting remain, but the closure loses the local sufficiency field requiring load-bearing context to survive and regime change to trigger re-estimation.


DERIVED CROSS-ORGANISM INVARIANTS


INV-2H.SruR-REVOCABLE-WARRANT — Continuity/equivalence is a revocable state, not a permanent label
Minimal body: 2H.SruR:wyz
Invariant: a continuity or equivalence warrant must carry its current operation, local quotient, evidence boundary and validity regime; when those conditions change, the warrant must be revalidated, narrowed or withdrawn rather than inherited automatically.
CREATE: state the current task/operation and the local transformation class proposed as nuisance.
COPY: carry the warrant together with its evidence and regime conditions across reconstruction rather than copying only its label.
CONTROL: test whether changed task, context or nuisance structure invalidates the old quotient or adequacy claim.
CULTIVATE: regenerate and widen the warrant only after the new regime survives revalidation.
Compression: A continuity claim is state with revocation conditions.


INV-2H.SruR-OPERATIONAL-RELATIONAL-REGENERATION — Regenerate relations, but witness operations
Minimal body: 2H.SruR:wxz
Invariant: bounded or changing internal state may preserve competence by regenerating a relational geometry only when the regenerated carrier preserves explicit task operations, retains context variables that can alter those operations, and passes an external recovery/adequacy witness.
CREATE: define the operational obligation and a reconstructive relational carrier.
COPY: regenerate the relation rather than demanding fixed-element identity.
CONTROL: preserve/ablate load-bearing context and test downstream operation plus external recovery.
CULTIVATE: allow carrier reorganization only while the operation remains witnessed under current conditions.
Compression: Regenerative geometry counts as continuity only through an operation-level local witness.


INV-2H.SruR-LOCAL-QUOTIENTED-RECONSTRUCTION — Reconstruction and quotienting share one local evidence boundary
Minimal body: 2H.SruR:xyz
Invariant: a reconstructed or compressed relational carrier may ignore representational differences only when those differences are locally warranted as nuisance and their removal preserves every distinction required for external recovery; regime change requires re-estimating both the quotient and the carrier's sufficiency.
CREATE: identify the relational structure to reconstruct and the candidate nuisance transformations.
COPY: retain independently meaningful factors and the local regime witness with the regenerated carrier.
CONTROL: perturb candidate nuisance dimensions and consequential context; reject quotient/compression when recovery changes.
CULTIVATE: simplify or broaden the carrier/quotient only as new regimes survive the same tests.
Compression: The same local witness licenses both what may be regenerated and what may be ignored.


METABOLITE-COLLAPSE PASS
Candidate claims reducible to a single parent were rejected: “continuity can be revalidated” is already carried by 1H.DUwl; “relations can survive changing realization” by 1H.2VF2; “equivalence is locally quotiented” by 1H.F8cX; and “validity is context-local” by 1H.8KP9. Pair claims that merely restated those parent conclusions were demoted. Three cross-organism metabolites survive collapse because revocable warrant, operation-witnessed relational regeneration, and local-quotiented reconstruction require distinct minimal multi-parent bodies and remain useful when either of the other two is removed.

volume.title: Reacquirable continuity reconstitution
volume.text:
Across all four parents, continuity can already survive changing realization without fixing one interior or canonical representation. The all-four closure adds a regenerative condition on the validity machinery itself. 2H._phq makes sparse current state lawful only while dormant source/evidence remains exactly reacquirable by stable role. 2H.Dp9x gives reconstruction a role-typed contract and demands end-to-end composite assurance in the regime where it is used. 2H.dxL5 makes portability pressure-tested rather than inferred from familiar form. 2H.AvDK turns continuity warrant into living state that can expire when regime or scaffold becomes insufficient.


The complete four-way closure is therefore reacquirable continuity reconstitution: a task-relevant public relation may remain continuous through selective activation, reconstruction, carrier/representation change and regime drift when its role-typed portable kernel travels with an evidence/validity boundary and a revocable continuity warrant while the omitted source/evidence body remains exactly reacquirable. Pressure or regime failure revokes the warrant; revocation must be able to reopen the implicated dormant evidence by stable role, regenerate the relation through the typed reconstruction contract, rerun composite and portability-pressure tests, and issue a new scoped warrant without rewriting what was previously warranted. Continuity here is not output similarity: it is a reversible warrant → reacquire → reconstruct → retest → rewarrant cycle whose historical evidence scopes remain distinct.
volume.invariant: A selectively realized public relation can count as continuous across changing carrier, representation and regime only while its exact obligation/evidence body remains reacquirable and its current continuity warrant remains revocable; when pressure or regime change invalidates that warrant, lawful continuation requires reopening the implicated dormant evidence, rebuilding through a role-typed reconstruction contract, retesting the composite and portable relation under current conditions, and issuing a newly scoped warrant rather than laundering the expired one into the repaired state.
removal: Remove 2H._phq: the closure loses exact dormant-source reacquisition and role-stable repair after revocation. The remaining trio can carry a typed, pressure-tested, revocable contract but cannot require a route back to support omitted from current realization.

Remove 2H.Dp9x: the closure loses the explicit role-typed reconstruction/transition contract and end-to-end composite assurance. The remainder can reacquire, pressure-test and revoke but cannot state the exact reconstruction obligation that must be re-earned.

Remove 2H.dxL5: the closure loses noncanonical portability and its dedicated pressure witness. The remainder can selectively reacquire, reconstruct and revise but lacks the stress surface that distinguishes portable continuity from familiar-carrier success.

Remove 2H.AvDK: the closure loses warrant-as-state and explicit revocation/revision conditions. The remainder can reacquire and pressure-reconstruct but cannot distinguish current legitimate continuation from an expired warrant requiring reconstitution.

3H.x3Cd.title: replayable continuity passport
3H.x3Cd.boundary: This child is a cross-holon relational synthesis over four already-metabolized 2H organisms. Their source evidence remains heterogeneous and separately bounded. Nothing here promotes operational correspondence into mechanism identity, stable interface behavior into ontology, reconstruction into sameness of interior state, or local validity into a universal guarantee. The child may only promote relations that require these complete parent bodies together; every inherited claim keeps its parent evidence, scope, non-identity and failure boundaries.

A failed pressure test revokes the old warrant while preserving the evidence needed to diagnose and rebuild it.

faces.text: 2H.AvDK + 2H.xqNz + 2H.Dp9x jointly earn a replayable portability kernel: an obligation-specific relation may cross carriers by preserving role semantics, evidence pointers, reconstructive scaffold and transition obligations rather than the whole old interior; after change, the relation is regenerated and tested as a fresh composite in the new regime, with dormant evidence available for revision if it fails.

volume.title: replayable continuity passport
volume.text:
All four parents together make the continuity warrant itself a portable, executable object rather than a descriptive label. 2H.AvDK contributes exact reacquisition of the evidence body, bounded regenerative scaffold and revision triggers. 2H.SruR contributes the locally licensed nuisance quotient and explicit revocation of continuity/equivalence when its admissibility conditions fail. 2H.xqNz contributes the obligation-minimal role-separated kernel, evidence/assurance boundary and pressure-aligned carrier variation that can falsify portability. 2H.Dp9x contributes lawful role-preserving transitions across representations and the requirement that each reconstructed target earn composite assurance in its current regime.


The complete closure is therefore a replayable continuity passport: a public relation may remain continuous through reconstruction, compression, quotienting and representation change without preserving one canonical interior when the traveling state carries (1) the role-typed operational obligation, (2) reconstructive scaffold plus exact evidence/reacquisition pointers, (3) the currently licensed nuisance quotient and local validity regime, (4) the transition obligations for lawful re-expression, and (5) an explicit pressure/revocation/replay procedure. A boundary-triggering change does not inherit the old warrant. The prior warrant remains historical evidence, while the new realization must replay acquisition, reconstruction, transition and pressure/composite tests and issue a newly scoped warrant before it may count as continued function.
volume.invariant: A continuity claim across changing realization is warranted only when its portable state can both reproduce the public obligation and reproduce the test of its own admissibility: it must carry the evidence/scaffold needed to reconstruct, the quotient/regime that states what differences are presently ignorable, the transition law that moves roles across carriers, and a pressure/composite witness capable of revoking and reissuing the warrant. Continuity that cannot replay why it still counts is not warranted continuity under this closure.
removal: Remove 2H.AvDK: the passport loses exact evidence/scaffold reacquisition and revision-triggered reconstruction; revocation and pressure can identify failure, but the state no longer earns a bounded route for replaying and repairing the warrant from its evidence body.

Remove 2H.SruR: the passport loses the explicit nuisance quotient and equivalence-revocation membrane; it can reconstruct, transport and pressure-test a relation, but cannot state which representational differences were lawfully ignored or when that permission expires.

Remove 2H.xqNz: the passport loses the obligation-minimal portable kernel, carrier-pressure witness and boundary-assurance discipline; reconstruction and transition remain locally testable, but portability itself is not challenged under the variation that should expose a false invariant.

Remove 2H.Dp9x: the passport loses the explicit role-preserving transition law and target-composite assurance; it can repair and pressure-test a local continuity warrant, but cross-representation re-expression is not earned as lawful continuity.

metabolites.title: PRESSURE-TRIGGERED-REISSUE
metabolites.text: when carrier pressure, regime change or quotient failure invalidates a portable continuity claim, the old warrant must remain historical evidence while the evidence/scaffold body is reacquired, the failed relation or quotient is rebuilt, and a newly scoped warrant is issued only after the relevant pressure test passes again.
metabolites.compression: failure should open a replay path, not erase its provenance.

metabolites.title: PORTABLE-REPLAY-KERNEL
metabolites.text: a portable continuity carrier may be smaller than its source interior only when it still carries the roles, evidence pointers, reconstructive scaffold and transition obligations required to regenerate the public relation and re-test the resulting composite in the target regime.
metabolites.compression: carry what lets both the relation and its test be replayed.

metabolites.title: EXECUTABLE-CONTINUITY-PASSPORT
metabolites.text: the right to call changing realizations continuous can itself be carried as executable state only when obligation, evidence/reacquisition body, quotient/regime, transition law and revocation/replay test travel together; after a boundary-triggering change, authority is re-issued by fresh composite evidence rather than inherited from the prior label.
metabolites.compression: continuity is portable only when the reason it still counts is portable too.

edges.title: Regime-typed portable kernel
edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies a locally valid reconstruction/transition family whose warrant changes with regime. 2H.dxL5 supplies the role-separated obligation kernel plus pressure-aligned and external sufficiency tests needed to establish portability. Together they earn a stricter relation: a portable kernel is not merely the smallest reproducible interface; it is a kernel whose admissible transformations and evidence boundary are explicitly indexed to the regime in which pressure tests show that the public obligation survives.
edges.removal:
without 2H.S5EU the kernel lacks an explicit regime-indexed transition/revalidation law; without 2H.dxL5 there is no independently earned obligation-specific portable kernel or pressure/external sufficiency witness.
Boundary: local validity does not imply universal portability, and passing one regime does not license neighboring regimes.

edges.title: Scaffold and transformation family must be co-revisable
edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies the rule that a reconstruction transition family must be re-estimated when its local validity regime changes. 2H.Dzmx supplies a role-separated reconstructible contract whose retained scaffold can become an obsolete stabilizing bias. Together they earn dual revision: continuity can fail because the scaffold is stale, because the transformation family is stale, or because both became mismatched, so a repair law must be able to revise both rather than protecting either as canonical.
edges.removal:
without 2H.S5EU the admissible transformation family has no explicit regime-sensitive revision law; without 2H.Dzmx there is no reconstructible contract/scaffold whose stabilizing history can become revision debt.
Boundary: co-revision is triggered by witnessed pressure or regime change, not by novelty preference.

edges.title: Regime change can require reacquisition before revalidation
edges.text: 2H.S5EU supplies regime-bounded validity and the obligation to re-estimate scaffold and transformation law when conditions change. 2H._phq supplies a still-reacquirable information body behind selectively active reconstruction, preventing omission from becoming irreversible deletion. Together they earn a repair path that neither parent supplies alone: when a regime change exposes a distinction absent from the current active scaffold, lawful revalidation may reopen dormant material before reconstructing the public relation rather than forcing the old compact carrier to answer a new obligation.
edges.removal:
without 2H.S5EU there is no regime-sensitive revalidation trigger; without 2H._phq there is no independently warranted dormant-body reachability from which omitted distinctions can be reacquired.
Boundary: regime change does not require global reload by default; reacquisition is required only where the current carrier or warrant proves insufficient.

edges.title: Pressure-certified reconstructible contract
edges.text: 2H.dxL5 supplies role-typed portable kernels, pressure-aligned carrier variation, external recoverability, and composite sufficiency tests. 2H.Dzmx supplies the reconstructible public contract and explicit scaffold-revision condition. Together they earn a contract whose compactness and continuity are certified by the pressure that could falsify them: a retained scaffold remains admissible only while independently varied carriers and end-to-end tests preserve the exact public obligation and its evidence boundary.
edges.removal:
without 2H.dxL5 there is no pressure/external/composite certification discipline; without 2H.Dzmx there is no explicit reconstructible contract or anchor-debt revision object to certify.
Boundary: pressure survival strengthens the scoped continuity claim only for the tested obligation and variation family.

edges.title: Selective portable kernel backed by a reacquirable whole
edges.text: 2H.dxL5 supplies an obligation-specific role-separated kernel whose portability must survive pressure-aligned and external tests. 2H._phq supplies selective activation over a larger body that remains stably reacquirable and carries the evidence boundary of omitted material. Together they earn reversible compactness: the active portable kernel may remain small while the obligation is satisfied, but the larger evidence/source body remains addressable so pressure can force the kernel to expand or be rebuilt when a previously dormant distinction becomes load-bearing.
edges.removal:
without 2H.dxL5 there is no tested obligation-specific kernel whose sufficiency can fail; without 2H._phq compactness can collapse into irreversible omission because the larger body need not remain reacquirable.
Boundary: a reachable larger body does not make the current compact kernel sufficient until the actual obligation is tested.

edges.title: Scaffold revision can reopen omitted body
edges.text: 2H.Dzmx supplies an explicit condition under which a stabilizing reconstructive scaffold must be reconsidered because it has become obsolete bias. 2H._phq supplies dormant source/evidence reachability outside the currently active reconstruction state. Together they earn revision by reopening rather than merely rearranging retained state: when the contract's current scaffold fails, the organism can reacquire previously omitted material and recompose the contract instead of treating its old information boundary as the universe of possible repair.
edges.removal:
without 2H.Dzmx there is no earned scaffold-bias/revision trigger; without 2H._phq there is no still-addressable omitted body that can participate in the revision.
Boundary: dormant material is a repair resource, not automatically relevant evidence; it must become load-bearing under the renewed obligation.

faces.title: Regime-bounded pressure-certified contract
faces.text: 2H.S5EU contributes regime-indexed reconstruction and transformation validity, 2H.dxL5 contributes role-separated portable kernels plus pressure/external sufficiency testing, and 2H.Dzmx contributes a reconstructible contract with scaffold-revision debt. Together they earn a contract whose present realization and permitted rewrite family are both provisional: continuity remains warranted only while pressure-aligned tests preserve the public obligation inside the current validity regime, and either scaffold or mapping may be revised when that warrant fails.
faces.removal: remove 2H.S5EU and the certification loses its explicit local-regime/transition-family boundary; remove 2H.dxL5 and pressure-aligned external/composite sufficiency testing disappears; remove 2H.Dzmx and there is no role-separated reconstructible contract with scaffold revision debt.

faces.title: Regime-bounded selective portability with reacquisition fallback
faces.text: 2H.S5EU contributes local validity and transition-family revalidation, 2H.dxL5 contributes the pressure-tested portable obligation kernel, and 2H._phq contributes selective active state backed by a still-reacquirable whole. Together they earn a sparse continuity architecture with an explicit fallback: operate through the compact kernel while it remains warranted, but when pressure or regime change exposes missing structure, reopen the dormant body, rebuild the necessary relation, and revalidate the transition rather than silently broadening the old kernel's authority.
faces.removal: remove 2H.S5EU and the fallback has no regime-indexed revalidation law; remove 2H.dxL5 and there is no pressure-tested portable kernel whose sufficiency is being assessed; remove 2H._phq and missing structure may be unrecoverable after selective omission.

faces.title: Reacquirable co-revision loop
faces.text: 2H.S5EU contributes revision of the admissible reconstruction/transition family under regime change, 2H.Dzmx contributes revision of a stabilizing scaffold when it becomes bias, and 2H._phq contributes dormant-body reacquisition. Together they earn a fuller repair loop: when continuity becomes locally invalid, reopen the evidence/source body as needed, revise both the retained scaffold and the transformation family, then reconstruct under a newly stated regime rather than preserving either old surface by default.
faces.removal:
remove 2H.S5EU and transformation/regime revision disappears; remove 2H.Dzmx and scaffold/contract revision disappears; remove 2H._phq and repair is confined to already-active state rather than being able to reopen omitted evidence.
Boundary: this face still lacks 2H.dxL5's independent pressure/external/composite certification that the repaired compact contract actually satisfies the public obligation.

faces.title: Pressure-tested continuity contract with reacquirable backing
faces.text: 2H.dxL5 contributes obligation-specific kernels and falsifying pressure/external tests, 2H.Dzmx contributes a reconstructible contract plus scaffold-revision condition, and 2H._phq contributes selective active state backed by a reacquirable whole. Together they earn a contract whose compact realization is reversible rather than lossy: pressure testing determines when the present kernel ceases to be sufficient, scaffold revision names the repair obligation, and dormant-body reacquisition supplies material that can re-enter before the contract is rebuilt.
faces.removal:
remove 2H.dxL5 and there is no independent pressure/external sufficiency witness; remove 2H.Dzmx and no explicit contract/scaffold revision object; remove 2H._phq and the repair cannot rely on preserved reachability beyond the active kernel.
Boundary: without 2H.S5EU this face does not yet earn an explicit regime-covariant law for the admissible transformation family itself.

volume.title: Reacquirable continuity renewal contract
volume.text:
Across all four parents, continuity becomes a renewable, evidence-bounded relation rather than persistence of one representation, one compact scaffold, or one once-issued warrant. 2H.S5EU shows that the validity of reconstruction and representation change is indexed to a local regime and that the admissible transformation family must be re-estimated as conditions change. 2H.dxL5 shows that the portable object can be a role-separated obligation kernel only while pressure-aligned, external, and composite tests demonstrate sufficiency. 2H.Dzmx shows that the persistent public object is a reconstructible contract whose stabilizing scaffold can itself become obsolete bias and therefore needs an explicit revision condition. 2H._phq shows that selective active state is faithful only while omitted source/evidence material remains reacquirable, so future repair is not trapped inside yesterday's compact view.


The complete four-way closure is therefore a reacquirable continuity renewal contract: a public relation may remain compact and selectively active across changing carriers only while its role-typed obligation, evidence boundary, current validity regime, scaffold, and admissible transition family jointly remain warranted under relevant pressure. When regime shift, pressure testing, or scaffold bias breaks that warrant, lawful continuation does not inherit the previous contract automatically. It reopens the still-reacquirable body where needed, revises both scaffold and transformation family, reconstructs the public relation, retests the exact obligation, and issues a newly bounded continuity contract while preserving the expired warrant as historical evidence rather than silently laundering it into the repaired state.
volume.invariant: A task-relevant continuity contract can remain compact and selectively active across changing internal realization only while a role-separated relational kernel, its evidence boundary, its current validity regime, and its admissible transition family remain pressure-tested as sufficient; when regime change or scaffold failure revokes that sufficiency, lawful renewal requires reacquiring any newly load-bearing dormant material, revising scaffold and transition law together, retesting the public obligation, and issuing a newly bounded warrant rather than inheriting the expired one.
removal: Remove 2H.S5EU: the closure loses explicit local-regime validity and the requirement that the admissible reconstruction/transition family itself be re-estimated under regime change.
Remove 2H.dxL5: the closure loses the obligation-specific portable kernel plus pressure-aligned, external, and composite sufficiency tests needed to certify renewal.
Remove 2H.Dzmx: the closure loses the reconstructible public contract and the explicit condition that a stabilizing scaffold can become obsolete bias requiring revision.
Remove 2H._phq: the closure loses the still-reacquirable dormant body and the rule that selective omission cannot become irreversible epistemic deletion.

metabolites.title: Revise the scaffold and the transformation family as one warranted pair
metabolites.text: when a continuity relation becomes invalid under regime or pressure change, repair must be able to revise both the reconstruction scaffold and the admissible transformation family because preserving either one as canonical can reproduce stale bias or an invalid mapping.
metabolites.compression: When continuity fails, yesterday's scaffold and yesterday's map are both revisable.

metabolites.title: Keep the active kernel small only while the larger body remains reopenable
metabolites.text: an obligation-specific compact kernel can remain selectively active without becoming lossy only when omitted source/evidence material stays reacquirable and relevant pressure tests are allowed to force expansion or reconstruction when a dormant distinction becomes load-bearing.
metabolites.compression: Sparse active state is safe only when missing truth can still come back.

metabolites.title: Continuity after revocation must be re-earned, not inherited
metabolites.text: after regime change, failed pressure testing, or scaffold bias revokes a continuity warrant, a repaired relation counts as renewed continuation only after the needed dormant body has been reacquired, scaffold and transition law have been revised as necessary, the exact public obligation has been retested, and a newly scoped warrant has been issued with the prior warrant retained as historical evidence.
metabolites.compression: A repaired relation does not inherit its old warrant; it earns a new one.

3H.UoYa.title: boundary-versioned continuity warrant lifecycle
3H.UoYa.boundary: This child is a cross-holon relational synthesis over four already-metabolized 2H organisms. Their underlying source lineages mix empirical, formal, architectural, operational, and conceptual evidence classes. Nothing at rank 3 upgrades those classes into a shared causal mechanism, substrate-independent ontology, or universal theorem. “Continuity,” “warrant,” “boundary,” “reconstruction,” “expansion,” “scope,” and “reissuance” remain operational relational terms bounded by the selected parent bodies and their inherited evidence limits.

edges.title: version-carrying reconstructive contract
edges.text:
2H.AvDK makes the continuity warrant itself part of living state and requires scaffold/regime revision when its assumptions fail. 2H.Dp9x makes the preserved obligation role-separated, transition-explicit, externally recoverable, and locally regime-typed. Together they earn a reconstructive contract whose current version includes not only what function must survive but also the scaffold assumptions, role semantics, transition law, evidence boundary, and conditions under which that exact contract remains sufficient.
Rank necessity: without 2H.AvDK, the role-separated contract can be revalidated but lacks the explicit “warrant-as-state” and scaffold-revision debt; without 2H.Dp9x, the revisable warrant lacks a typed cross-representation role/transition contract and composite reconstruction assurance.

edges.title: audited revocation threshold
edges.text:
2H.AvDK supplies a warrant that can expire when scaffold or regime becomes insufficient. 2H.MKvK supplies the independent distinction between better access/reallocation and genuine expansion across a prior boundary. Together they earn a specific revocation threshold: not every realization change invalidates the current warrant; revocation is triggered when evidence shows that the active scaffold/regime is insufficient or that a claimed capability change actually crosses the boundary the current warrant was scoped to.
Rank necessity: without 2H.AvDK, boundary evidence has no explicit stateful warrant/scaffold to revoke; without 2H.MKvK, warrant revision lacks the audited distinction between within-boundary elasticity and true boundary change.

edges.title: reissuable warrant state
edges.text:
2H.AvDK says the continuity warrant travels as state and must be revised rather than silently inherited when its regime or scaffold changes. 2H.KcdR says a verified boundary crossing changes the scope of that warrant and requires a new source/active partition, transition/interface obligations, and evidence boundary while preserving the old warrant as history. Together they earn versioned reissuance: a new warrant is not an overwrite of the old one but a successor state with a larger or altered declared scope and explicit provenance back to the expired contract.
Rank necessity: without 2H.AvDK, reissuance lacks the explicit warrant-as-state and scaffold/revision substrate; without 2H.KcdR, revision lacks the concrete scope-transition law and historical preservation of the expired warrant.

edges.title: elastic transition assurance
edges.text:
2H.Dp9x supplies role-separated, operation-preserving transitions plus independent composite assurance. 2H.MKvK supplies elastic carrier variation and the audit separating changed access from enlarged support. Together they earn an assurance law for elastic transitions: carrier, representation, or routing may change inside the current scope without creating a new continuity version when the named roles/operations remain sufficient and external relation tests still pass; a claimed expansion remains a separate question requiring its own boundary witness.
Rank necessity: without 2H.Dp9x, elasticity lacks an explicit transition/role contract and independent end-to-end assurance; without 2H.MKvK, successful transitions can be confused with growth of the reachable support.

edges.title: scope-versioned operational passport
edges.text:
2H.Dp9x carries a regime-typed operational contract across reconstruction and representation change. 2H.KcdR requires that contract to be reissued after a separately witnessed expansion, with previous evidence retained as provenance. Together they earn a passport whose validity is both operational and scope-versioned: it can authorize lawful movement among carriers inside a witnessed regime, but when the support boundary changes the passport must be reissued rather than merely stamped as if its original scope were unchanged.
Rank necessity: without 2H.Dp9x, reissuance lacks the role-separated transition and external-recovery obligations that make the passport executable; without 2H.KcdR, the passport has no explicit scope-transition/reissue law after genuine expansion.


zy — stress-confirmed expansion handoff
2H.MKvK supplies pressure-aligned testing that distinguishes reallocation/access effects from actual crossing of the prior support boundary. 2H.KcdR supplies the post-crossing handoff that rebuilds the source/active partition, transition obligations, interface, and evidence boundary for the enlarged regime. Together they earn a two-stage expansion handoff: first prove that the old boundary was genuinely crossed under relevant stress; only then retire the prior continuity authorization and initiate a reissued contract for the enlarged field.
Rank necessity: without 2H.MKvK, the handoff can be triggered by mere access/reallocation effects; without 2H.KcdR, confirmed expansion lacks the explicit reissue procedure that makes the enlarged state lawfully continuous.

faces.title: audited reconstructive continuity version
faces.text: 2H.AvDK + 2H.Dp9x + 2H.MKvK jointly earn a current continuity version that is reconstructive, role/transition explicit, and boundary-audited. The carrier may change elastically while the same version remains in force only if its scaffold assumptions, role/operation obligations, external relation tests, and regime conditions continue to pass and no independent boundary witness shows that the scope itself has changed.
faces.removal: remove 2H.AvDK and the version loses warrant-as-state plus scaffold-revision debt; remove 2H.Dp9x and it loses typed transition roles and composite assurance; remove 2H.MKvK and it loses the explicit access-versus-expansion audit.

faces.title: reconstructive warrant succession
faces.text: 2H.AvDK + 2H.Dp9x + 2H.KcdR jointly earn a succession law for continuity contracts. A bounded reconstructive warrant can travel across representations as an executable role/transition contract, but when verified scope change forces reissue the next warrant must carry forward the source/evidence ancestry, declare its changed assumptions and scope, and re-earn end-to-end assurance rather than retroactively extending the predecessor.
faces.removal:
remove 2H.AvDK and the succession loses stateful scaffold/warrant revision; remove 2H.Dp9x and it loses an executable role-separated transition contract and external reconstruction test; remove 2H.KcdR and it loses explicit scope-change reissuance plus historical predecessor preservation.


wzy — revocation-to-reissue continuity cycle
2H.AvDK + 2H.MKvK + 2H.KcdR jointly earn the state transition from a valid current warrant to an expired historical warrant and then to a newly issued successor. A changed realization first has to be classified against the old boundary; if the old scaffold/regime is merely perturbed but still sufficient, the warrant may remain after revalidation. If a genuine boundary crossing or scaffold/regime insufficiency is witnessed, the old warrant is revoked as current authority, retained as provenance, and a successor warrant must be constructed and retested.
Removal tests: remove 2H.AvDK and there is no explicit living warrant/scaffold state to revoke; remove 2H.MKvK and the transition lacks a discriminating boundary audit; remove 2H.KcdR and revocation lacks the structured reissue/historical handoff into a successor scope.


xzy — boundary-versioned portability
2H.Dp9x + 2H.MKvK + 2H.KcdR jointly earn portable continuity whose authorization is versioned by support boundary. Within a version, role-separated operations may be reconstructed and translated across carriers while external tests preserve assurance. Across a verified expansion boundary, the transition family and public interface must be retested and reissued for the new scope. Thus portability is neither surface sameness nor unlimited reuse of an old contract.
Removal tests: remove 2H.Dp9x and portability loses role/transition semantics plus reconstruction assurance; remove 2H.MKvK and there is no independent boundary audit distinguishing elasticity from enlargement; remove 2H.KcdR and the enlarged scope has no explicit reissue law.

volume.title: boundary-versioned continuity warrant lifecycle
volume.text:
All four parents together earn an explicit lifecycle for continuity authority rather than a static continuity predicate.


2H.AvDK contributes warrant-as-state: the current right to call reconstruction “continued function” includes scaffold assumptions, evidence/reacquisition boundaries, and a validity regime that can itself become insufficient. 2H.Dp9x contributes the executable content of that warrant: role-separated operational obligations, lawful representation transitions, externally recoverable reconstruction, and composite assurance. 2H.MKvK contributes the change classifier: elastic carrier movement, routing, reweighting, or better access remains inside the existing scope until an independent pressure-aligned witness demonstrates that the prior support boundary has actually been crossed. 2H.KcdR contributes the succession law: once expansion changes scope, the old authorization becomes historical provenance and a new source/active partition, transition/interface contract, and evidence boundary must be reissued and retested.


The complete closure is therefore a boundary-versioned continuity warrant lifecycle. Continuity authority has a current version with declared obligation, role/transition semantics, reconstruction scaffold, evidence/reacquisition boundary, regime, and support boundary. Ordinary within-boundary carrier change can preserve that version when its tests remain satisfied. Scaffold failure, regime invalidation, or verified boundary expansion can revoke its current authority. A successor version is then issued only after the changed scope and obligations are reconstructed, retested, and witnessed, while the predecessor remains preserved as provenance. This makes change classification, revocation, and reissuance part of the continuity object itself rather than external bookkeeping.
volume.invariant: A continuity claim remains lawfully reusable only while its current version can state what must survive, reconstruct or translate that obligation across admissible carriers, recover the evidence/baseline needed to audit it, and distinguish within-scope elasticity from events that invalidate or enlarge its scope. When that boundary is genuinely crossed or the scaffold/regime becomes insufficient, the existing warrant expires as current authority but persists as history; continued use requires a newly witnessed successor warrant whose changed scope is explicit.
removal: Remove 2H.AvDK: the closure loses warrant-as-state, scaffold debt, and the explicit ability for the continuity authorization itself to become a revisable object.
Remove 2H.Dp9x: the closure loses the role-separated executable contract, lawful transitions, external reconstruction witness, and composite assurance that make each warrant version operational.

Remove 2H.MKvK: the closure loses the independent classifier separating ordinary elastic change or better access from genuine boundary expansion, so version transitions can be triggered by the wrong kind of change.
Remove 2H.KcdR: the closure loses the explicit succession/reissuance law that preserves expired authority as provenance and rebuilds the contract for the enlarged scope.

metabolites.title: CHANGE-CLASSIFICATION-GATE
metabolites.text: before modifying a continuity warrant, classify the observed change against both scaffold/regime sufficiency and the prior support boundary. Carrier movement, rerouting, reweighting, or reacquisition may remain within the current version; genuine boundary expansion or scaffold/regime insufficiency is a revocation event.
metabolites.compression: classify the change before changing the warrant.

metabolites.title: VERSIONED-CONTINUITY-WARRANT
metabolites.text: continuity authority is versioned state containing an operational obligation, role/transition contract, reconstruction scaffold, evidence/reacquisition boundary, validity regime, and declared support scope. A current version may survive admissible carrier change, but revoked versions become immutable provenance rather than being rewritten to fit later scope.
metabolites.compression: preserve not just continuity, but which continuity warrant is current and why.

metabolites.title: EXPANSION-HANDOFF-PROTOCOL
metabolites.text: confirmed boundary expansion requires a two-stage handoff: prove the crossing under stress against the prior baseline, then reissue and retest the role/operation/interface contract for the enlarged regime before the new state inherits continuity authority.
metabolites.compression: expansion changes the scope; the handoff earns the next warrant.
